company.name: Corning Energy Corporation
company.subsector: Regulated natural gas and electric distribution
company.ownershipVehicle: ACP Crotona Holdings, L.P. / ACP Crotona Corp.
company.description: Corning Energy Corporation is the parent platform for regulated natural gas and electric distribution utilities in New York and Pennsylvania, including Corning Natural Gas Corporation, Pike County Light & Power Company and Leatherstocking Gas Company. Pike is an operating subsidiary rather than a separate manager-level infrastructure investment. Corning's operating history dates to 1904, its holding company was formed in 2013, and it acquired all of Pike's stock from Orange & Rockland on August 31, 2016. Argo Infrastructure Partners completed the acquisition of 100% of the Corning parent platform on July 6, 2022 through the ACP Crotona ownership chain. A 2025 application proposed replacing the Argo general partner with an Apollo-controlled general partner, but the transaction did not close and was terminated in January 2026. Argo therefore remains the current owner, and no signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 16, 2026.

milestones.event: Corning Natural Gas, the principal regulated utility operating company and predecessor of the current Corning Energy platform, was incorporated.
Pike County Light & Power Company, now a regulated operating subsidiary of Corning Energy, was incorporated in Pennsylvania.
Corning Natural Gas Holding Corporation was formed as the public parent of Corning Natural Gas and its utility investments; it was later renamed Corning Energy Corporation.
Corning Natural Gas Holding Corporation acquired all outstanding stock of Pike County Light & Power from Orange & Rockland Utilities, adding Pike as a regulated subsidiary.
Argo Infrastructure Partners completed the acquisition of 100% of Corning's common and preferred stock through the ACP Crotona ownership chain.
The Pennsylvania PUC held a hearing on an application for an indirect change of control of Corning Energy and its Pike and Leatherstocking subsidiaries involving Apollo and Argo-affiliated entities.
Argo, ACP Crotona Holdings and Apollo withdrew the New York petition after the proposed general-partner transaction failed to close and was terminated.

company.name: Black Hills Colorado IPP, LLC
company.ownershipVehicle: AIA Energy North America LLC / AIA Colchis LLC
company.description: Black Hills Colorado IPP, LLC is the manager-level independent-power investment within the broader Pueblo Airport Generating Station in Pueblo County, Colorado. The full site totals 440 MW, but the IPP company owns the 200 MW combined-cycle facility that entered service in 2012; the other 240 MW is utility-owned and is not part of Argo's investment. Black Hills Electric Generation retains a 50.1% controlling interest and the operating role, while Argo Infrastructure Partners manages the AIA Energy North America structure whose AIA Colchis vehicle holds the remaining 49.9%. AIA signed for the interest on February 12, 2016 and closed on April 14, 2016. The IPP sells capacity and energy to Black Hills Colorado Electric under a contract running through December 31, 2031. Black Hills' August 2026 filing continued to report the IPP noncontrolling interest, and no Argo/AIA exit or signed pending IPP ownership transfer was identified through August 16, 2026.

milestones.event: The 200 MW combined-cycle facility owned by Black Hills Colorado IPP commenced commercial operation within the broader Pueblo Airport generating site.
Black Hills signed a definitive agreement to sell a 49.9% member interest in Black Hills Colorado IPP for $215 million to Argo-managed AIA Energy North America LLC.
AIA Energy North America completed the 49.9% acquisition; Black Hills retained its 50.1% controlling interest and continued to operate the IPP facility.

Black Hills' second-quarter filing continued to report distributions to the Black Hills Colorado IPP noncontrolling interest; its separate NorthWestern parent merger remained pending and no IPP-level ownership transfer was reported.
Black Hills discloses that the agreement under which the 200 MW IPP provides capacity and energy to Black Hills Colorado Electric runs through December 31, 2031.

The portfolio totals 377 MW and has produced approximately 1.4 million MWh in an average year. Brookfield acquired the former Alcoa Tapoco assets in 2012. company.name: UGI Utilities – Electric Division
company.description: UGI Utilities – Electric Division is a regulated electric transmission, distribution and retail utility serving more than 63,000 customers in Luzerne and Wyoming counties in northeastern Pennsylvania. The business operates approximately 2,700 miles of transmission and distribution lines and 14 substations. UGI Utilities, Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of UGI Corporation, remains the current legal owner. Funds managed by Argo Infrastructure Partners LP signed an approximately $470 million definitive purchase agreement on April 28, 2026, but UGI's August 2026 Form 10-Q continued to classify the business as held for sale and expected closing in UGI fiscal Q2 2027, subject to customary closing conditions and applicable regulatory approvals. The exact Argo fund, manager-level stake, standalone legal suffix, headquarters, founding year and separate website are not publicly disclosed. Wyoming Valley Electric Holdings LLC and related acquisition entities are transaction vehicles for this same target, not separate PortCos. No legal close, termination, resale or revised timetable was identified through August 16, 2026.

UGI Utilities, Inc. and Wyoming Valley Electric Holdings LLC filed their joint Federal Power Act section 203 application in FERC docket EC26-118-000.

company.name: US Water Systems
company.description: US Water Systems is an unsupported repository umbrella for two separate municipal water and wastewater concession investments: the Bayonne water and wastewater concession in New Jersey and Middletown Water Joint Venture LLC in Pennsylvania. SUEZ and New York regulatory materials describe the concessions separately, and Water Capital Partners' current project list does the same; no reviewed source identifies a legal US Water Systems entity or one operating platform above both investments. Argo acquired KKR and SUEZ interests in the two concession SPVs in 2017, while Veolia/SUEZ remained the operator and minority participant. Current municipal, operator and project records show both concessions remain active. Apollo's announced acquisition of the Argo manager did not close and was terminated in January 2026, so Apollo never became an owner of the assets. This umbrella record is archived from the manager-level PortCo census without a redirect to prevent double counting; the separate Bayonne and Middletown records remain published. No later sale, concession termination, signed pending exit or ownership transfer was identified through August 16, 2026.

milestones.event: Bayonne entered a 40-year water and wastewater concession with a KKR and United Water consortium; the concession is a separate canonical investment rather than part of a legal US Water Systems platform.
Middletown Borough executed its separate long-term water and wastewater concession agreement with Middletown Water Joint Venture LLC.
KKR and SUEZ transferred their respective interests in the separate Bayonne and Middletown concession SPVs to Argo Infrastructure Partners; SUEZ retained minority operating interests.
Middletown Borough's operating report documented continued active water and wastewater system operations under the separate Middletown concession.

A New York regulatory filing confirmed that Apollo's proposed acquisition of the Argo manager had not closed and that the agreement and transaction were terminated, creating no concession-level ownership change.

company.name: Waihonu Solar Farm
company.description: Waihonu Solar Farm is the collective name for Waihonu North Solar, a 5.0 MW photovoltaic plant, and Waihonu South Solar, a 1.5 MW photovoltaic plant, in Mililani on Oʻahu. The operating projects comprise 26,232 modules on approximately 12 acres and sell electricity to Hawaiian Electric under a power purchase agreement. Argo Infrastructure Partners acquired Waihonu as an underlying asset in its July 21, 2022 purchase of Hawaiʻi Gas and related businesses. Hawaiʻi Gas states that a solar energy provider acquired Waihonu in 2025, and the 2025 early-release Form EIA-860 data reports ERCAM LLC as the utility and operator for both plants. The projects remain operational, but no reviewed source establishes ERCAM as an infrastructure-fund manager. Waihonu is therefore realized and archived from the manager-level PortCo census without a redirect; Hawaiʻi Gas remains a distinct published platform. The exact 2025 closing date, transaction value and ERCAM parent are not publicly disclosed, and no later sale or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 16, 2026.

company.name: ACL Airshop
company.subsector: Air cargo ULD leasing and logistics infrastructure
company.description: ACL Airshop is a global air-cargo unit load device platform that leases, pools, sells, repairs, tracks and manages ULDs and supplies pallets, containers, nets, straps and related cargo-control equipment. Headquartered in Greenville, South Carolina, the company served more than 200 airlines, air-cargo carriers and other transportation clients and owned, maintained or managed more than 100,000 ULDs across 55 airport hubs as of March 2026. The business was founded as Airline Container Leasing in 1983 and its successor operations merged with AirShop Holdings in 2007. Alinda-managed funds completed the acquisition in April 2021; the manager renamed its mid-market infrastructure strategy Astatine Investment Partners in 2022. A January 2023 prospectus states that Alinda Infrastructure Fund IV held a 100% equity interest, while current Astatine sources reaffirm ownership without restating the percentage. No later sale, recapitalization, merger, sponsor change or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 17, 2026. Airport stations, ULD fleets, repair sites, software and products are operations or assets within ACL Airshop, not separate PortCos.

company.name: Virginia International Gateway
company.description: Virginia International Gateway is the private owner of the highly automated VIG marine container terminal in Portsmouth, Virginia. The terminal handles containerized cargo for ocean carriers, beneficial cargo owners, railroads, motor carriers and regional supply chains; Astatine describes approximately 2 million TEU of annual throughput capacity. Virginia International Gateway, Inc. owns the terminal, the Virginia Port Authority leases it under a long-term facilities lease, and the authority's Virginia International Terminals subsidiary operates it. The facility opened in 2007 as APM Terminals Virginia. Affiliates of Alinda-managed funds and USS acquired it in August 2014 and renamed it VIG. Astatine now lists one VIG profile as Active and a separate Fund II investment as exited in 2019. The Virginia Port Authority's August 2025 final official statement identifies USS and PSP as the current underlying owners, supporting an active Astatine manager attribution and an active PSP direct-owner association while preserving the realized Fund II period. The active Astatine fund or managed-account vehicle, manager-level stake and entry date, plus PSP's entry date and percentage, are not publicly disclosed. No later full sale, signed pending exit or transfer of terminal title to the port authority was identified through August 18, 2026. APM Terminals Virginia is the predecessor name; VPA, VIT, lease interests, bonds, cranes and expansion projects are not separate PortCos.

company.name: DataBank
company.description: DataBank Holdings, Ltd. operates a nationwide digital-infrastructure platform providing colocation, interconnection, cloud, storage, managed security and compliance services to enterprise, cloud, content and technology customers. Founded in Dallas in 2005, DataBank was acquired from Avista by a DigitalBridge-led group in July 2016 and has since expanded through acquisitions, development and multiple recapitalizations. DataBank reported more than 70 data centers in more than 25 markets, 20 interconnection hubs, more than 2,200 customers and more than $1 billion of revenue in May 2026. The current manager-universe ownership roster is DigitalBridge, Swiss Life Asset Managers, IMCO, AustralianSuper, Northleaf Capital Partners, Ardian and CBRE Investment Management. DigitalBridge disclosed a 7.8% continuing stake after the January 2025 secondary. TIAA's Real Estate Account separately disclosed a 14.8% beneficial stake through DigitalBridge Zeus vehicles; DataBank brands that relationship as Nuveen, but it is not evidenced as a Nuveen Infrastructure investment. EDF Invest and TJC are also current investors outside the supplied manager universe. Individual data centers, campuses, interconnection hubs and acquired operating assets remain within the single DataBank platform boundary. No later full sale or signed pending exit was identified through August 18, 2026.

milestones.event: DataBank Ltd. was founded in the former Federal Reserve Bank Building in downtown Dallas, Texas.
Digital Bridge acquired DataBank from Avista Capital Partners with TIAA, Allstate Investments and The Edgewater Funds, launching its first data-center platform.

Colony Capital purchased $185 million of secondary DataBank interests from Edgewater and Allstate; Edgewater exited, Allstate retained half of its prior interest and the Nuveen-branded TIAA investment continued.

A Swiss Life-led consortium with EDF Invest, Northleaf and Ardian closed a collective 35% DataBank interest for approximately $1.5 billion; IMCO then agreed to invest up to $450 million in the continuing recapitalization.

DataBank announced an approximately $2.0 billion equity raise led by AustralianSuper's $1.5 billion commitment, which would make AustralianSuper a significant minority owner; DataBank now lists it as a current investor.

DataBank announced a $250 million TJC investment and an approximately $600 million secondary share sale; DigitalBridge disclosed that the transaction would adjust its continuing DataBank stake to 7.8%.

company.name: Transurban Chesapeake
company.description: Transurban Chesapeake LLC is the concession platform that owns the entities operating the 495, 95 and 395 Express Lanes in Northern Virginia, including the Fredericksburg Extension and 495 NEXT. It develops, finances, operates and maintains dynamically priced express lanes serving motorists, high-occupancy vehicles, buses and permitted commercial traffic in partnership with VDOT. At June 30, 2026, Transurban reported 50% ownership, AustralianSuper 25%, CPP Investments 15% and UniSuper 10%; only AustralianSuper and CPP Investments are tracked infrastructure-manager owners here. The 495 concession covered 26.5 kilometres and the 95/395/FredEx concession 79 kilometres, each running through December 2087. No platform sale, secondary transfer or signed pending exit was identified through August 18, 2026. Chesapeake Partnership and Chesapeake toll road network are aliases for the same manager-level platform; individual roads and extensions are components, not separate PortCos.

milestones.event: The 395 Express Lanes opened to traffic as part of the Chesapeake managed-lanes platform.

CPP Investments announced a 15% Chesapeake interest on December 16 and AustralianSuper announced a 25% interest on December 17; UniSuper agreed to acquire 10% and Transurban would retain 50%.
Transurban completed the sale of a 50% interest in Transurban Chesapeake to AustralianSuper, CPP Investments and UniSuper on March 31, 2021; reporting became effective April 1.
VDOT and Transurban opened the 10-mile 95 Express Lanes Fredericksburg Extension to mainline traffic.

company.name: Axium Extendicare LTC II LP
company.description: Axium Extendicare LTC II LP is the Ontario-Manitoba long-term-care ownership platform that succeeded AXR Operating (National) LP and the relevant portion of the former Revera-Axium joint venture. At June 30, 2026, it owned 26 operating homes with 3,502 beds; Axium held 85% through Axium LTC Limited Partnership, while Extendicare held a 15% managed interest and operated the homes. The platform serves residents requiring provincially regulated long-term care and receives operating, management and procurement services from Extendicare. Arbour Heights is a 174-bed Kingston home beneath this platform, not a separate PortCo. The original venture formed in 2017 at 75% Axium and 25% Revera, separated its western assets into an AgeCare-Axium venture in 2022, and became Axium Extendicare LTC II LP when Extendicare acquired Revera's remaining 15% Ontario-Manitoba interest in 2023. No later platform sale or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 18, 2026.

milestones.event: Revera and Axium formed the joint venture and completed its first acquisition of 16 long-term-care homes; Axium held 75% and Revera 25%.

Revera and Axium completed the 32-home long-term-care platform in 2018 after forming the joint venture and closing the first 16 homes on December 21, 2017; the second 16-home Ontario acquisition closed April 27, 2018.
The Revera-Axium platform expanded beyond its original 32-home portfolio when Arbour Heights became its first external acquisition.
The Axium-Revera joint venture acquired Arbour Heights, a 174-bed long-term-care home in Kingston, Ontario.
Revera sold its 15% interest in certain Alberta and British Columbia homes to AgeCare, separating the western assets into a distinct AgeCare-Axium joint venture.
Extendicare acquired Revera's remaining 15% Ontario-Manitoba interest; AXR Operating (National) LP became Axium Extendicare LTC II LP, with Axium retaining 85%.

company.name: Axium Aster & Axium Bloom
company.description: Axium Aster & Axium Bloom is Axium Infrastructure's combined manager-level investment in two Canadian long-term-care property portfolios. Axium's current portfolio materials report 26 operating facilities and 4,114 beds across Alberta and British Columbia, with cash flows supported by provincially licensed, regulated and funded long-term-care and continuing-care frameworks plus resident co-payments. Axium owns 92.5% of each portfolio; AgeCare owns the 7.5% balance and operates the facilities. Aster began in 2020 as a five-facility, 1,402-bed Alberta partnership at 80% Axium and 20% AgeCare. Bloom traces to the western tranche of the Revera-Axium joint venture that first closed in 2017; Revera sold its remaining 15% interest in certain Alberta and British Columbia homes to AgeCare in 2022. Individual homes are underlying assets, and the separately presented 16-home Ontario Axium Iris portfolio is outside this company boundary. No Axium exit or signed pending sale was identified through August 18, 2026.

canonicalAfterImage.name: Axium Aster & Axium Bloom
canonicalAfterImage.description: Axium Aster & Axium Bloom is Axium Infrastructure's combined manager-level investment in two Canadian long-term-care property portfolios. Axium's current portfolio materials report 26 operating facilities and 4,114 beds across Alberta and British Columbia, with cash flows supported by provincially licensed, regulated and funded long-term-care and continuing-care frameworks plus resident co-payments. Axium owns 92.5% of each portfolio; AgeCare owns the 7.5% balance and operates the facilities. Aster began in 2020 as a five-facility, 1,402-bed Alberta partnership at 80% Axium and 20% AgeCare. Bloom traces to the western tranche of the Revera-Axium joint venture that first closed in 2017; Revera sold its remaining 15% interest in certain Alberta and British Columbia homes to AgeCare in 2022. Individual homes are underlying assets, and the separately presented 16-home Ontario Axium Iris portfolio is outside this company boundary. No Axium exit or signed pending sale was identified through August 18, 2026.

company.name: Edwards Sanborn Solar + Storage
company.ownershipVehicle: Axium ES Holdings LLC / AxInfra US LP
company.description: Edwards Sanborn Solar + Storage is Axium Infrastructure's manager-level holding across the operating EdSan 1A and EdSan 1B utility-scale solar and battery-storage phases in Kern County, California. Axium's current portfolio reports 346 MW of solar and 1,339 MWh of storage for 1A and 358 MW of solar and 1,497 MWh of storage for 1B, while the transaction releases disclose 397 MWac / 1,505 MWh and 410 MWac / 1,497 MWh nameplate figures respectively. The projects serve utility, municipal-utility and corporate counterparties under long-term revenue contracts. Phase 1A closed with Axium at 80% and Terra-Gen at 20%; Phase 1B closed with Axium ES Holdings at 50% and Terra-Gen at 50%. AxInfra US LP owns 92.26% of Axium Co-Invest Holdings, the upstream co-invest holding company. No synthetic combined-company ownership percentage is inferred, no direct source identifies AxInfra Fund I-IV as the owning fund, and no later Axium sale or signed pending exit was identified through August 18, 2026.

milestones.event: Axium disclosed Phase 1A transaction-era scale of 397 MWac of solar capacity and 1,505 MWh of battery storage, with 346 MWac at the point of interconnection.
Axium ES Holdings completed its acquisition of 80% of the Phase 1A project companies from Terra-Gen; Terra-Gen retained 20%.
Axium ES Holdings completed its acquisition of 50% of the voting interests in the Phase 1B sellers; Terra-Gen retained the other 50%.
Axium publicly announced its Phase 1B investment and described Phases 1A and 1B as a combined 807 MWac solar and 3,002 MWh storage complex.
Axium's live portfolio continued to list Axium ES Holdings LLC as one current operating holding covering EdSan1A and EdSan1B.

company.name: Etobicoke Healthcare Partnership
company.description: Etobicoke Healthcare Partnership LP is the availability-based design-build-finance-maintain project company for the Etobicoke General Hospital Phase 1 Patient Tower in Toronto, Ontario. The C$330 million project added an approximately 250,000-square-foot, four-storey clinical tower. Axium Infrastructure Canada II L.P. and DIF Infrastructure IV through DIF Infra 4 Canada Ltd. were the equity sponsors at the May 2016 financial close. Construction reached substantial completion on February 19, 2019. William Osler Health System's audited statements for the year ended March 31, 2026 continue to identify Etobicoke Healthcare Partnership as responsible for operating and maintaining the building, with project assets transferring to Osler in July 2048. Exact sponsor percentages are not publicly disclosed, and no later project-level sponsor sale or signed pending exit was identified through August 18, 2026.

The Phase 1 Patient Tower reached substantial completion and entered its operating phase.

William Osler Health System's audited statements continued to identify Etobicoke Healthcare Partnership as responsible for operating and maintaining the building, with project assets transferring to Osler in July 2048.

company.name: Montreal Gateway Terminals Partnership
company.ownershipVehicle: Fiera Axium Infrastructure Canada II L.P.
company.description: Montreal Gateway Terminals Partnership is a common-user marine container terminal operator at the Port of Montreal. It operates the Cast and Racine terminals as one intermodal platform, providing vessel, yard, reefer, storage, gate and rail/truck-transfer services to global shipping lines and cargo owners serving Canada and the U.S. Midwest and Northeast. The Port of Montreal reports effective handling capacity of 800,000 TEU at Cast and 500,000 TEU at Racine. A consortium led by Fiera Axium Infrastructure acquired 100% of the business from Morgan Stanley Infrastructure Partners on March 5, 2015; Fiera Axium Infrastructure Canada II L.P. was the disclosed Axium vehicle, but Axium's individual stake was not published. Axium's live portfolio continues to list the asset as operational. A 2025 debt refinancing identified FA MGT Limited Partnership as the parent but did not transfer equity. Public evidence reviewed did not support carrying the other 2015 consortium members forward as confirmed active owner rows, and no later sale or signed pending exit was found through August 18, 2026. Termont Montreal, the Port authority, and the individual Cast and Racine terminals are not separate companies within this record.

Morgan Stanley Infrastructure Partners increased its ownership from 80% to 100%.
The consortium led by Fiera Axium Infrastructure completed its 100% acquisition from Morgan Stanley Infrastructure Partners; Fiera Axium Infrastructure Canada II L.P. was the disclosed Axium vehicle.
Montreal Gateway Terminals pursued a C$440 million senior-secured note refinancing through its FA MGT holding structure; the financing did not represent an equity transfer.

company.name: PUC Transmission LP
company.ownershipVehicle: Axium Infrastructure Canada II Limited Partnership / Axium TransCo LP
company.description: PUC Transmission LP is an Ontario regulated transmitter developing, financing, constructing and operating Tagona West Transformer Station and an approximately 10 route-kilometre, dual-circuit 230 kV transmission line in Sault Ste. Marie. The approximately C$230 million project will provide about 300 MW of new load to Algoma Steel's electric-arc-furnace operations while strengthening regional reliability and capacity. The line comprises approximately 20 circuit-kilometres across two 400 MVA circuits. Axium Infrastructure holds 80% through the disclosed Axium Infrastructure Canada II Limited Partnership / Axium TransCo chain, while PUC Inc. retains 20%. The OEB granted leave to construct on August 27, 2024 and issued electricity transmission licence ET-2021-0088 on April 10, 2025. Current company materials target construction completion in Q1 2028 and energization in January 2028. No later ownership transfer or signed pending exit was identified through August 18, 2026.

milestones.event: PUC Transmission was incorporated to develop and operate transmission infrastructure in Sault Ste. Marie.
The Ontario Energy Board issued electricity transmission licence ET-2021-0088 after the October 2021 conditional approval and August 2024 leave-to-construct decision.
Axium Infrastructure announced that a managed fund had acquired an 80% equity interest in PUC Transmission LP; PUC Inc. retained the 20% balance.
The Ontario Energy Board granted PUC (Transmission) LP leave to construct Tagona West Transformer Station and its 230 kV transmission line.
PUC selected S.&T. Electrical to build the transmission line and station and reported a Q1 2028 completion target.

company.name: Fatbeam
company.ownershipVehicle: Basalt IV / Project Lighthouse AIV Feeder LP
company.description: Fatbeam is a Coeur d'Alene, Idaho-based owner-operator of fiber networks serving commercial, education, healthcare, government, carrier, tower, residential and multifamily customers across Arizona, Idaho, Montana, Nevada, New Mexico, Oregon, Washington and Wyoming. company.name: Cleco Corporate Holdings LLC
company.subsector: Regulated electric utility and wholesale generation
company.description: Cleco Corporate Holdings LLC is the operating parent within the privately held Cleco Group utility platform, serving Louisiana through Cleco Power and related generation assets. The regulated utility serves approximately 298,000 customers across 24 Louisiana parishes and owns eight generating units with 2,676 MW of rated capacity, supported by transmission and distribution networks and approved tariffs. Macquarie Asset Management, BCI and Manulife completed the take-private acquisition on April 13, 2016 and remain the legal owners; their last publicly confirmed 2020 interests were 53.9%, 36.9% and 9.2%, respectively, while exact current percentages are not publicly disclosed. A signed agreement announced April 27, 2026 would sell 100% of Cleco Group to Pine JV Holdings LLC, backed by Stonepeak and Bernhard Capital Partners, but the regulatory proceedings remained open through August 19, 2026, so the existing owners remain active pending closing.

company.name: GCT Global Container Terminals Inc.
company.description: GCT Global Container Terminals Inc. is a Canadian marine-terminal operator serving containerized trade through the Port of Vancouver. The platform operates GCT Deltaport in Delta and GCT Vanterm in Vancouver, providing vessel, yard, gate, on-dock rail and truck-appointment services to ocean carriers, rail and trucking partners, logistics providers and cargo owners. Current company materials report four berths and nearly 3.5 million TEUs of annual capacity. Ontario Teachers' established the platform in 2007; IFM Investors and BCI joined in 2018, producing the current 37.5%, 37.5% and 25% ownership split. The U.S. terminals were sold to CMA CGM in 2023, leaving the two-terminal Canadian scope. No later ownership transfer or signed pending platform sale was identified through August 19, 2026.

Mosaic launched on November 1, 2018. company.name: Nexus Water Group, Inc.
company.description: Nexus Water Group, Inc. is a regulated water and wastewater utility platform formed when the U.S. regulated operations of Corix Infrastructure combined with SouthWest Water Company on April 1, 2024. The business operates locally branded systems across the United States and Canada and serves more than 1.3 million people. BCI owns 50.0% through its Infrastructure & Renewable Resources program. The other 50% is held through SWMAC Holdco, producing indirect platform interests of 37.5% for J.P. Morgan Asset Management's Infrastructure Investments Fund and 12.5% for a Munich Re vehicle managed by MEAG. Nexus completed the sale of systems in eight states to American Water on June 1, 2026, while its announced Nevada and Oregon asset sale remained pending; neither transaction is a sponsor sale or platform exit.

milestones.event: The U.S. regulated water and wastewater businesses of Corix Infrastructure and SouthWest Water combined to form Nexus Water Group.
BCI's Corix interests and the IIF/Bazos-backed SouthWest platform completed their combination, establishing the 50% BCI and 50% SWMAC ownership structure.

company.description: Puget Energy, Inc. is a Bellevue, Washington-based utility holding company whose core business is Puget Sound Energy, the regulated electric and natural gas utility serving western Washington. PSE is wholly owned by Puget Energy and serves approximately 1.26 million electric customers and 883,000 natural-gas customers across roughly 6,000 square miles in 10 counties. Puget LNG is a separate nonregulated subsidiary of Puget Energy. The platform is owned through Puget Holdings by BCI (20.9%), Macquarie Asset Management (15.8%), OMERS (23.9%), Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan (15.8%), AIMCo (13.6%) and PGGM (10.0%). No later sponsor transfer or signed pending platform sale was identified through August 23, 2026. Puget Sound Energy is retained as the regulated subsidiary and operating brand rather than counted as a separate PortCo.

company.ownershipVehicle: Mariana US Aggregator, L.P. through the AI Infrastructure Partnership
company.description: Aligned Data Centers develops and operates hyperscale and build-to-suit data center campuses for cloud, AI, high-performance-computing and enterprise customers. Founded in 2013 and headquartered in Dallas, the platform reported 51 campuses and more than 6.4 GW of operational and planned capacity across the United States and Latin America at the July 2026 transaction closing. On July 21, 2026, an AI Infrastructure Partnership consortium led by Global Infrastructure Partners and MGX completed its acquisition of 100% of Aligned at an enterprise value of approximately US$40 billion. GIP/GIM and MGX are the current joint controllers; their exact percentages and underlying fund allocations are not publicly disclosed. Macquarie Asset Management-managed funds and Mubadala were direct owners before the closing and are preserved as former owners. BlackRock is shown only as GIP's parent, AIP only as the investment program and Mubadala only as an indirect parent of MGX. No later ownership transfer or signed exit was identified through August 23, 2026.

company.description: ALLETE, Inc. is a Duluth, Minnesota-based utility holding company whose businesses include Minnesota Power, Superior Water, Light and Power, ALLETE Clean Energy, BNI Energy, New Energy Equity and other energy infrastructure interests. Its regulated utility footprint is concentrated in Minnesota and Wisconsin, with clean-energy activities across North America. The take-private announced in May 2024 closed on December 15, 2025, and ALLETE survived as a privately held company under Alloy Parent LLC. CPP Investments owns 40% indirectly and Global Infrastructure Partners-managed vehicles own the remaining 60% indirectly, comprising GIP Fund V and the GIP-managed Tower Bridge vehicle. BlackRock is shown only as GIP's parent, not as a separate owner. Regulatory filings in 2026 describe a pending internal reorganization around Minnesota Power, not a completed ownership transfer. No later owner exit or signed platform sale was identified through August 23, 2026.

company.name: Bluepoint Wind
company.description: Bluepoint Wind, LLC is the holder of federal offshore-wind lease OCS-A 0537 in the New York Bight, approximately 38 nautical miles from New York and 53 nautical miles from New Jersey. The 71,522-acre lease supported a pre-construction concept of up to 2.4 GW but no generation facilities were constructed. Bluepoint Winds Holdings, LLC owns the leaseholder and is itself owned 50:50 by Ocean Winds through OW North America LLC and Global Infrastructure Partners through Seaway Energy Holdings, L.P. BlackRock is shown only as GIP's parent, while Mubadala's undisclosed participation remains within the GIP block. On April 27, 2026, the project parties signed a settlement that suspended lease duties and provides for cancellation after specified investment verification and reimbursement steps. BOEM still describes that cancellation as conditional; no final cancellation, ownership transfer or dissolution was identified through August 23, 2026, so both legal owner periods remain active.

milestones.event: The federal offshore-wind lease for the Ocean Winds and Global Infrastructure Partners project became effective after their joint venture won the New York Bight auction; Bluepoint's parent remained owned 50:50 through OW North America and Seaway Energy Holdings.

Bluepoint and the U.S. Department of the Interior signed a settlement suspending lease duties and providing for future cancellation after specified verification and reimbursement steps; cancellation was not yet complete.

canonicalAfterImage.description: Bluepoint Wind, LLC is the holder of federal offshore-wind lease OCS-A 0537 in the New York Bight, approximately 38 nautical miles from New York and 53 nautical miles from New Jersey. The 71,522-acre lease supported a pre-construction concept of up to 2.4 GW but no generation facilities were constructed. Bluepoint Winds Holdings, LLC owns the leaseholder and is itself owned 50:50 by Ocean Winds through OW North America LLC and Global Infrastructure Partners through Seaway Energy Holdings, L.P. BlackRock is shown only as GIP's parent, while Mubadala's undisclosed participation remains within the GIP block. On April 27, 2026, the project parties signed a settlement that suspended lease duties and provides for cancellation after specified investment verification and reimbursement steps. BOEM still describes that cancellation as conditional; no final cancellation, ownership transfer or dissolution was identified through August 23, 2026, so both legal owner periods remain active.

company.name: CleanCapital Holdings, LLC
company.description: CleanCapital Holdings LLC develops, acquires, owns and operates distributed solar and energy-storage projects across the United States. Founded in 2015 and headquartered in New York, the platform serves commercial, industrial, institutional, utility and public-sector counterparties through contracted clean-energy assets. Current company materials report more than 350 projects and approximately 500 MW, with over US$1.5 billion invested. BlackRock Renewable Power Group funds made a direct investment in 2019, but that period is historical and the exact stake and exit date are not publicly disclosed. Manulife Investment Management made a corporate investment in 2021 and remains the only named current institutional backer; its exact percentage is not publicly disclosed. BlackRock's acquisition of GIP did not create a GIP ownership period. CleanCapital sold the 120 MW Nottingham development in April 2026 as an asset-level transaction and no platform sale or signed exit was identified through August 23, 2026.

milestones.event: CleanCapital was founded.

CleanCapital acquired a 40-asset, 22.7 MW portfolio from Kendall Sustainable Infrastructure and secured further equity investment.
CleanCapital announced the acquisition of a 25 MWh storage portfolio from Pacifico.

company.name: Clearway Energy Group
company.ownershipVehicle: Global Infrastructure Partners III via Zephyr Holdings, L.P.
company.description: Clearway Energy Group LLC is a U.S. developer, owner and operator of wind, solar, battery-storage and flexible generation assets. Founded as an independent platform in 2018 and headquartered in San Francisco, Clearway currently reports approximately 13.6 GW of gross capacity across 27 states. The company serves utilities, corporate and institutional buyers, governments, community-choice aggregators and other power-market customers, largely through contracted generation. Global Infrastructure Partners acquired the predecessor NRG renewables platform in 2018 through GIP III entities. On September 12, 2022, TotalEnergies closed its purchase of 50% of Clearway from GIP, leaving GIP III and TotalEnergies as equal current owners. BlackRock is shown only as GIP's parent after the 2024 manager acquisition and Evergreen Infrastructure Fund has no Clearway ownership period. Listed affiliate Clearway Energy, Inc. remains a separate company. No later platform sale or signed ownership change was identified through August 23, 2026.

company.name: Electrada
company.ownershipVehicle: BlackRock Climate Infrastructure; exact vehicle not publicly disclosed
company.description: Electrada, LLC was a U.S. commercial fleet-charging platform that financed, owned and managed charging infrastructure under charging-as-a-service arrangements. Launched in 2020 and headquartered in Cincinnati, the company served commercial, institutional and public fleets through no-upfront-capex infrastructure and energy-management contracts. BlackRock Climate Infrastructure backed Electrada beginning in 2021, but the exact fund, vehicle and stake were not publicly disclosed. On April 20, 2026, Current Trucking acquired Electrada's operating, construction and development assets, more than 30 sites, customer agreements and select personnel. On June 17, 2026, Inspiration Mobility acquired select remaining assets, team, pipeline, depot-development capability, energy software and intellectual property. Those transactions ended Electrada as a standalone operating platform; neither buyer is treated as a full legal successor and no GIP ownership period exists.

milestones.event: Electrada launched its electric-fleet charging platform.
BlackRock Climate Infrastructure led Electrada's Series B financing; the exact fund, legal vehicle and stake were not publicly disclosed.

Current Trucking acquired Electrada's operating, construction and development assets in April, and Inspiration Mobility acquired select remaining assets, team, pipeline, software and intellectual property in June, ending the standalone platform.

company.name: Environmental 360 Solutions
company.description: Environmental 360 Solutions is a North American waste-management and environmental-infrastructure platform serving municipal, commercial and industrial customers. Founded in 2018 and headquartered in Aurora, Ontario, E360S provides collection, transfer, recycling, special and liquid waste, emergency response and industrial-cleaning services. Current company materials report more than 800,000 customers across Alberta, British Columbia, Ontario, Quebec, Saskatchewan and Michigan. BlackRock Global Infrastructure Fund IV closed a majority acquisition on February 16, 2023. Founder Donato Ardellini retained a significant stake and Canadian Business Growth Fund retained and increased its minority position; exact percentages are not publicly disclosed. OPTrust and Oaktree exited at the 2023 closing. BlackRock's acquisition of GIP did not create a separate GIP ownership period. E360S entered the United States through a Michigan acquisition announced in July 2026, and no later platform sale or signed exit was identified through August 23, 2026.

milestones.event: Environmental 360 Solutions was founded.
BlackRock Global Infrastructure Fund IV closed its majority acquisition; Donato Ardellini and Canadian Business Growth Fund retained ownership, while OPTrust and Oaktree exited.

company.name: Electrada
company.ownershipVehicle: BlackRock Climate Infrastructure; exact vehicle not publicly disclosed
company.description: Electrada, LLC was a U.S. commercial fleet-charging platform that financed, owned and managed charging infrastructure under charging-as-a-service arrangements. Launched in 2020 and headquartered in Cincinnati, the company served commercial, institutional and public fleets through no-upfront-capex infrastructure and energy-management contracts. BlackRock Climate Infrastructure backed Electrada beginning in 2021, but the exact fund, vehicle and stake were not publicly disclosed. On April 20, 2026, Current Trucking acquired Electrada's operating, construction and development assets, more than 30 sites, customer agreements and select personnel. On June 17, 2026, Inspiration Mobility acquired select remaining assets, team, pipeline, depot-development capability, energy software and intellectual property. Those transactions ended Electrada as a standalone operating platform; neither buyer is treated as a full legal successor and no GIP ownership period exists.

BlackRock Climate Infrastructure led Electrada's Series B financing; the exact fund, legal vehicle and stake were not publicly disclosed.

company.name: Eolian
company.subsector: Renewable project development and battery storage
company.description: Eolian is a U.S. renewable-power and battery-storage investment, development and operating platform formed in 2020 from MAP Energy's renewable business. It develops, funds, owns and operates utility-scale battery storage, finances renewable projects and retains operating-project royalties while serving utilities, independent power producers, wholesale markets and large industrial and data-center loads. GIP reports operating-project royalties across 19 GW, while Eolian reports nearly 30 GW cumulatively funded or developed; neither figure represents wholly owned capacity. GIP IV acquired MAP RE/ES in 2020 and GIP continues to classify Eolian as unrealized. Eolian's July 2026 Flint Grid announcement identifies employees and GIP-managed funds as current owners. BlackRock's 2024 acquisition of the GIP manager did not create a separate Eolian ownership period. Eolian is the counted platform; Astral and project SPVs are underlying assets, and the 2021 Able Grid transaction concerned development-portfolio interests rather than Able Grid itself.

milestones.event: GIP announced GIP IV's acquisition of 100% of MAP Energy's renewable-energy business, which became Eolian; the exact legal closing date was not publicly disclosed.
Eolian acquired the remaining interests in Able Grid-managed joint-venture development portfolios; it did not acquire Able Grid Energy Solutions itself.

company.name: Lighthouse
company.subsector: Commercial and industrial distributed solar and solar-plus-storage
company.description: Lighthouse is a portfolio of 38 operating commercial-and-industrial distributed solar and solar-plus-storage projects totaling 89 MWDC across California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Minnesota, Vermont and Washington. The portfolio is asset-heavy and contracted, with operating renewable-generation and storage assets serving long-term commercial and industrial offtakers. BlackRock's Evergreen infrastructure strategy signed to acquire Lighthouse in November 2023 and the sale closed in December 2023. Excelsior Energy Capital sold 100% of its membership interests in the portfolio through Excelsior Renewable Energy Investment Fund I LP and disclosed the completed exit in March 2024. The transaction disclosure does not establish that BlackRock owns 100% of every project's total economic interests, so the current platform-level percentage is not inferred. Lighthouse is counted once as the manager-level portfolio; its 38 underlying project and SPV assets are not separate PortCos. No later portfolio sale, transfer or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 23, 2026.

company.name: Gigapower
company.description: Gigapower, LLC is a U.S. wholesale open-access fiber platform formed as a 50/50 joint venture between AT&T and a BlackRock-origin infrastructure vehicle. The company builds, owns and operates multi-gigabit fiber networks that multiple internet service providers can use to serve homes and businesses outside AT&T's traditional wireline footprint. Regulatory filings identify AT&T-related Infrastructure Endeavors Holdings, LLC and Teleport Communications America, LLC as holding an aggregate 50% interest and BGIF IV Neon Acquisition LP as holding the other 50%. The predecessor entity formed in Delaware in February 2022, changed its name to Gigapower in March 2022, and the joint venture closed and launched in May 2023. Current disclosures describe availability or expansion in Florida, New Mexico, northeastern Pennsylvania, North Carolina, South Carolina and southeastern Minnesota, with a long-term target of roughly 1.5 million customer locations. GIP, part of BlackRock, is now referenced as the fund manager, but no separate asset-level transfer or second GIP ownership period was disclosed.

AT&T and BlackRock closed the joint venture and launched Gigapower as an open-access fiber platform.

company.name: Harquahala Generation Company
company.ownershipVehicle: BlackRock Global Energy & Power Infrastructure Fund III
company.description: Harquahala Generation Company is the manager-level record for New Harquahala Generating Company, LLC, owner of a 1,092 MW combined-cycle natural-gas generation facility in Maricopa County, Arizona. The plant supplies wholesale energy, capacity and grid-reliability services and is 100% tolled through 2031 with an undisclosed investment-grade utility. Capital Power operates, maintains and manages the facility. Capital Power and BlackRock announced a 50/50 acquisition from CSG Investments in November 2023 and closed the purchase on February 16, 2024. BlackRock invested through its Global Energy & Power Infrastructure Fund III Trident structure. Capital Power's 2025 annual report and Q2 2026 report continued to show the 50% joint-venture interest and operating facility. The plant began commercial operation in 2004; that date is not treated as the legal company's founding year. No later sale, ownership transfer or signed pending exit was identified through August 23, 2026.

company.name: Indian Energy
company.ownershipVehicle: BlackRock Impact Opportunities bridge loan for the Viejas project; debt-only and repaid
company.description: Archived PortCo-census record for Indian Energy, LLC, an active Native American-owned developer, integrator, owner and operator of resilient microgrids, renewable generation and energy storage. Indian Energy is a qualifying infrastructure operating company, but no direct BlackRock or GIP equity ownership was established. The relationship previously recorded as a BlackRock GEPIF III ownership period was instead an approximately US$25 million BlackRock Impact Opportunities bridge loan supporting the Viejas Enterprise Microgrid project. Indian Energy identified BlackRock Impact Opportunities as a financing partner at the September 2024 project financial close, and a direct 2026 BlackRock Impact Opportunities interview said the bridge capital had earned a return and been returned. A July 2024 tribal-government resolution separately disclosed a 15% direct Indian Energy interest held by the Sault Ste. Marie Tribe. The complete current cap table is not public, but the evidence is sufficient to exclude the company from the requested BlackRock and GIP PortCo lists. The record is archived rather than represented as a realized infrastructure-fund equity investment.

company.name: Jupiter Power
company.description: Jupiter Power LLC is a U.S. utility-scale battery-energy-storage platform that develops, owns and operates BESS projects serving energy, capacity and ancillary-services markets. Current company materials report 8,800 MWh operating, under construction or under contract and more than 20,000 MW in active development across eight U.S. RTO/ISO markets. BlackRock's legacy Diversified Infrastructure business announced the acquisition of Jupiter from EnCap Investments and co-investors Yorktown Partners and Mercuria Energy on November 15, 2022, and the acquisition closed on December 21, 2022. Jupiter now uses GIP-backed branding following BlackRock's October 2024 acquisition of GIP, but no separate Jupiter asset transfer or second GIP ownership period was disclosed. company.name: Portland Natural Gas Transmission System
company.description: Portland Natural Gas Transmission System is a standalone FERC-regulated natural-gas transmission business serving New England and Atlantic Canada. The approximately 295-mile system crosses New Hampshire, Maine and Massachusetts, connects with Canadian pipelines and has nearly 460,000 dekatherms per day of capacity. Its customers include utilities, energy marketers, industrial users and power generators. BlackRock- and Morgan Stanley Infrastructure Partners-managed funds announced the acquisition from TC Energy and Énergir on March 4, 2024 and closed it on August 15, 2024 for approximately US$1.14 billion including assumed notes. Regulatory evidence identifies BlackRock Global Infrastructure Fund IV and North Haven Infrastructure Partners III as equal 50% indirect owners through Beehive Loop AcquisitionCo LLC. The former owners' 61.7% and 38.3% direct interests ended at closing. PNGTS maintains a corporate office in Houston and an operating office in Lancaster, New Hampshire. No later company sale or signed pending exit was identified through August 23, 2026.

milestones.event: Portland Natural Gas Transmission System entered service as an interstate transmission link between Canadian supply and New England markets.
TC Energy and Énergir agreed to sell PNGTS to BlackRock- and MSIP-managed funds for approximately US$1.14 billion including US$250 million of assumed notes.
The sale closed, establishing BlackRock Global Infrastructure Fund IV and North Haven Infrastructure Partners III as equal 50% indirect owners through Beehive Loop AcquisitionCo LLC.
New Hampshire regulators approved the ownership transfer and documented the two acquiring funds' equal indirect interests.
A Federal Register notice documented continuing PNGTS operations and its Houston corporate office while the pipeline pursued a blanket-certificate project request.

company.description: Revolution Wind & South Fork Wind is a paired manager-level record for two separate contracted U.S. offshore-wind project companies: Revolution Wind, LLC and South Fork Wind, LLC. South Fork is a 132 MW, 12-turbine project serving Long Island that entered commercial operation on March 14, 2024. Ørsted retains the other 50% of each project, and Eversource is retained as the former 50% partner. company.name: Rio Grande LNG
company.description: Rio Grande LNG is a large-scale LNG liquefaction and export terminal under construction at the Port of Brownsville, Texas. NextDecade operates the project, which is planned for approximately 30 million tonnes per annum across five trains and serves global long-term LNG offtakers. Phase 1 closed on July 12, 2023 with equity from Global Infrastructure Partners, GIC, Mubadala, TotalEnergies and NextDecade. The same investor group participated in later Train 4 and Train 5 transactions through separate project vehicles. XRG subsequently acquired partial GIP interests: 11.7% of Phase 1 and 7.6% across Trains 4 and 5. GIP remains an active investor after those partial sell-downs. BlackRock's October 2024 acquisition of GIP did not create a separate Rio Grande LNG ownership period. At June 2026, Trains 1 and 2 were 74.0% complete, Train 3 was 50.4%, Train 4 was 15.5% and Train 5 was 9.4%, with first Train 1 LNG expected in the first half of 2027. Train and holding entities are treated as project vehicles beneath the one terminal record. No signed pending company-level exit was identified through August 23, 2026.

milestones.event: Rio Grande LNG reached Phase 1 final investment decision and closed the joint-venture equity transaction with GIP, GIC, Mubadala, TotalEnergies and NextDecade.
The Train 4 equity transaction closed with NextDecade at 40%, GIP at 36.9%, TotalEnergies at 10%, GIC at 7.9% and Mubadala at 5.2% at entry.
XRG completed its acquisition of an 11.7% indirect Phase 1 interest from a GIP vehicle, reducing but not eliminating GIP's ownership.
The Train 5 equity transaction closed with NextDecade at 50%, GIP at 36.9% and GIC/Mubadala holding a combined 13.2% at entry.
XRG completed a second acquisition from a GIP vehicle, taking a 7.6% aggregate interest across Trains 4 and 5 while GIP retained a residual stake.
NextDecade reported Trains 1 and 2 at 74.0% completion, Train 3 at 50.4%, Train 4 at 15.5% and Train 5 at 9.4%, with first Train 1 LNG expected in the first half of 2027.

company.name: Saavi Energía
company.description: Saavi Energía is a Mexico-based power-generation and gas-infrastructure platform serving wholesale, commercial and industrial electricity users and gas-services customers. The platform operates more than 3.7 GW across six combined-cycle plants, one solar plant, three gas-compression stations, three mobile turbines and a 40-mile pipeline. Actis formed Saavi from the InterGen México business in 2018 and sold 100% of the platform to Global Infrastructure Partners in August 2021 through GIP's emerging-markets infrastructure program. GIP remains the current legal owner. On April 27, 2026, GIP signed an agreement to combine Saavi with Grupo México power assets; if it closes, Grupo México would own 70% and GIP 30%. No legal closing was identified through August 23, 2026.

company.name: STRATOS
company.description: STRATOS is a direct-air-capture and geologic-sequestration infrastructure project in Ector County, Texas, owned through a joint venture between Occidental and a fund managed by legacy BlackRock Diversified Infrastructure. Occidental develops and operates the project through 1PointFive and consolidates the venture; BlackRock is the active noncontrolling infrastructure investor and committed $550 million at entry in November 2023. The facility is designed to capture up to 500,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide per year and use three permitted Class VI wells for permanent saline sequestration. Public sources do not disclose the owners' exact economic percentages, the BlackRock fund name, a separate STRATOS headquarters, or a legal commercial-operation date. No sale or signed ownership transfer was found through August 23, 2026.

company.name: The AES Corporation
company.subsector: Electric utilities and global power generation
company.description: The AES Corporation is a publicly traded, U.S.-headquartered power and utilities company with regulated utilities, conventional generation, renewable energy, battery storage and related infrastructure across the United States and international markets. Its customers include regulated residential, commercial and industrial utility users, corporate and technology buyers, utilities and wholesale-market counterparties. AES remained publicly owned as of August 23, 2026. A consortium jointly controlled by GIP-managed vehicles and EQT Infrastructure VI signed an agreement on March 1, 2026 to acquire 100% of AES through Horizon Parent, L.P.; CalPERS and QIA are also participants. Stockholders approved the merger and the HSR waiting period expired in June 2026, but other regulatory reviews remained open and no legal closing was found. GIP, EQT, CalPERS and QIA are therefore pending buyers, not current owners.

milestones.event: Applied Energy Services, Inc., now The AES Corporation, was incorporated.
AES announced a definitive agreement for a GIP- and EQT-led consortium to acquire 100% of the company through Horizon Parent, L.P.
AES stockholders approved the merger after the HSR waiting period expired; other regulatory approvals and legal closing remained pending.

company.name: Vanguard Renewables
company.subsector: Anaerobic digestion and renewable natural gas
company.ownershipVehicle: BlackRock Global Energy & Power Infrastructure Fund III
company.description: Vanguard Renewables is a U.S. anaerobic-digestion and renewable-natural-gas platform that processes food and agricultural waste for farms, food and beverage companies, waste generators and energy buyers. The company develops, owns and operates farm digesters, gas-upgrading systems and related organics infrastructure across the Northeast, Midwest and Southeast, with nationwide development activity. BlackRock Real Assets acquired the business from Vision Ridge Partners on July 20, 2022 through Global Energy & Power Infrastructure Fund III; current GIP branding reflects BlackRock's upstream 2024 acquisition of GIP, not a second Vanguard ownership transfer. Ingka Investments completed a minority investment in September 2025. CMA CGM/PULSE announced another minority investment in August 2025, but no legal closing was found through August 23, 2026.

company.name: Vopak Industrial Infrastructure Americas
company.ownershipVehicle: BlackRock Global Energy & Power Infrastructure Fund III
company.description: Vopak Industrial Infrastructure Americas, LLC is a contracted industrial-terminal and bulk-liquid-storage platform on the U.S. Gulf Coast. Its Freeport, St. Charles and Plaquemine sites provide tank storage and marine, pipeline, rail and truck logistics under long-term service agreements, with Dow as the disclosed anchor customer. Royal Vopak and BlackRock's Global Energy & Power Infrastructure Fund III formed the 50/50 joint venture and completed the $620 million acquisition of the three terminals from Dow on December 2, 2020. The terminals are nested operating sites beneath one VIIA PortCo. BlackRock's October 2024 acquisition of GIP did not create a separate VIIA ownership period, and no later sale or signed pending ownership transfer was found through August 23, 2026.

company.ownershipVehicle: Blackstone Energy Transition Partners IV (BETP IV)
company.description: Advanced Cooling Technologies (ACT) designs and manufactures thermal-management components and systems, including two-phase cooling, heat pipes, phase-change materials, cold plates and environmental-control units. The Lancaster, Pennsylvania-based platform serves data centers, advanced computing, defense, space, electronics, medical, industrial and HVAC markets, with additional integrated operations in York, Pennsylvania and Anaheim, California. Blackstone Energy Transition Partners announced a majority investment on March 11, 2026 and the transaction closed on May 19, 2026 through BETP IV; the exact percentage and management rollover are not publicly disclosed. ACT announced more than $5 million of additional capacity investment, a planned 50,000-square-foot facility and up to 100 new jobs in July 2026. No later sale, transfer or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 23, 2026.

company.description: Arlington Industries manufactures electrical fittings, connectors, boxes, enclosures, cable-management, grounding, communications, security and audio-visual products for electrical distributors and contractors serving commercial, industrial, data-center, communications and building applications. The company operates from a seven-acre manufacturing base in Scranton, Pennsylvania, with regional distribution in the United States and Canada, and reported more than 350 North American patents or applications in its 2024 company history. Blackstone Energy Transition Partners announced an acquisition agreement on January 26, 2026; the FTC identifies Blackstone Energy Transition Partners IV AIV L.P. as the acquirer, and Blackstone's second-quarter 2026 results report Arlington within capital deployed. The exact closing date, stake and any Stark-family rollover are not publicly disclosed. No later sale or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 23, 2026.

company.description: Sabre Industries engineers and manufactures transmission and distribution structures, wireless towers and components, integrated enclosures and related products for power utilities, telecommunications operators and data-center developers. company.name: TXNM Energy
company.description: TXNM Energy, Inc. is the Albuquerque, New Mexico-based public holding company above regulated electric utilities Public Service Company of New Mexico and Texas-New Mexico Power. The platform serves residential, commercial and industrial customers in New Mexico and Texas through rate-regulated generation, transmission and distribution infrastructure. The corporation was incorporated in 2000, established its holding-company structure in 2001 and changed its name from PNM Resources to TXNM Energy in August 2024. Blackstone Infrastructure signed an agreement on May 19, 2025 to acquire 100% of TXNM. A separate $400 million PIPE for eight million shares closed on June 2, 2025, but a New Mexico order caused those shares to be cancelled and the investment repaid on July 22, 2026. TXNM therefore remains publicly owned while the take-private remains signed and pending regulatory approvals. No specific final Blackstone fund allocation or legal closing date is publicly disclosed.

company.name: Duke Energy Florida
company.description: Duke Energy Florida, LLC is a regulated electric utility providing generation, transmission, distribution and retail power service to about two million residential, commercial and industrial customers across approximately 13,000 square miles in central and western Florida. Its operating utility lineage dates to 1899. Brookfield's first subscription closed on March 3, 2026 through Peninsula Power Holdings L.P., giving Brookfield a 9.19% indirect non-controlling interest through Duke Energy Florida's parent, Florida Progress, LLC; Duke retained 90.81% and operating control. Additional signed subscriptions may increase Brookfield's interest to as much as 19.7%, but no later closing was verified through August 19, 2026. Florida Progress is treated as the transaction holdco rather than a separate PortCo. The current LLC's formation year and Brookfield's allocation among individual BSIP commitment entities are not publicly disclosed.

The first subscription closed for approximately $2.8 billion, giving Brookfield a 9.19% indirect non-controlling interest while Duke retained 90.81% and operating control.

company.name: CAG Holdings
company.description: CAG Holdings is Carlyle's U.S. airport infrastructure platform associated with The New Terminal One at John F. Kennedy International Airport. The related project company, JFK NTO LLC, is developing, financing, constructing and will operate a roughly $9.5 billion, 2.6 million-square-foot international terminal with 23 gates under a long-term Port Authority lease. Carlyle originally held a 51% indirect project interest; at financial close on June 10, 2022, Ferrovial acquired 96% of that position and Carlyle retained approximately 2% indirect ownership. Ferrovial's 2026 SEC materials report the current project split as Ferrovial 49%, Carlyle 2%, JLC Infrastructure 30% and Ullico Infrastructure 19%. CAG remains the manager-level PortCo; JFK NTO LLC and the terminal are the associated project rather than separate PortCos. No later Carlyle full exit or signed divestiture was found through August 19, 2026. CAG's platform-level stake, precise legal entry date and current headquarters are not publicly disclosed.

The consortium reached financial close and full notice to proceed; Ferrovial acquired 96% of Carlyle's former 51% project interest, leaving Carlyle with approximately 2% indirect ownership.
Ferrovial reported the terminal at 92% construction progress, with 32 airline agreements and Phase A beneficial occupancy targeted for March 2027.

Carlyle launched Copia as a wholly owned platform in 2021 and later combined it with Birch Infrastructure's renewable-energy business. Carlyle and EQT announced a signed agreement on July 9, 2026 for EQT Infrastructure VII to acquire Copia, but the transaction remained subject to customary conditions and no closing was verified through August 19, 2026. company.description: Fermata Energy LLC was a Charlottesville, Virginia-based vehicle-to-grid technology and services business founded in 2010. company.description: Accelerate Infrastructure Opportunities, LLC (AIO) owns and manages land and ground leases beneath digital, renewable-energy and transportation/electrification infrastructure in the United States, including telecom, data-center, fiber, billboard, wind, solar, storage and EV-charging or logistics sites. The business was founded in 2016 and launched its dedicated CBRE Investment Management-backed infrastructure-site strategy in December 2022. Accelerate Investment Partners began operating as AIO on March 9, 2026 without a change to the platform, team or strategy. On May 7, 2026, AIO closed a $630 million primary raise that added Mubadala and Australian Retirement Trust capital and brought total equity commitments to approximately $1.26 billion. CBRE IM reported more than 450 sites across 47 states by July 2026. CBRE IM remains the sponsor and Mubadala is a current platform-equity co-investor; their exact percentages and complete legal vehicle mapping are not publicly disclosed. No later platform sale, exit or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 23, 2026.

company.name: Vantage Data Centers
company.description: Vantage Data Centers develops, owns, manages and operates hyperscale data-center campuses for cloud, AI, internet and large-enterprise customers. Founded in 2010 and headquartered in Denver, the global platform includes substantial United States and Canadian operations. This canonical record consolidates direct platform equity and manager-level North American co-investments while treating Vantage SDC as a stabilized 12-asset North American portfolio managed and operated by Vantage rather than as a separate company. DigitalBridge has held platform equity since the March 2017 acquisition and led the closed $9.2 billion 2024 recapitalization with Silver Lake. CBRE participated first in pre-SDC platform equity and then in the current Vantage SDC portfolio; DigitalBridge separately retains a 12.8% SDC interest. Pantheon Infrastructure plc has a current $34.7 million North American co-investment, GCM Grosvenor retains its disclosed growth-platform exposure, and PSP exited the North American and EMEA development platforms in 2024 while disclosing a residual Vantage interest. Exact post-2024 platform percentages, most vehicles, CBRE's SDC percentage, Pantheon's closing date and PSP's residual layer are not publicly disclosed. No signed Vantage sale or later ownership transfer was identified through August 23, 2026.

CBRE Caledon completed its investment in the Vantage SDC stabilized portfolio after rolling or selling its pre-SDC platform interests into the new structure.
Pantheon Infrastructure plc announced a $34.7 million direct co-investment in Vantage's North American data-center business.
Vantage closed a $9.2 billion equity investment led by DigitalBridge and Silver Lake; PSP exited the North American and EMEA development platforms while retaining another Vantage interest.

company.name: Gateway Fiber
company.ownershipVehicle: Sponsored fund and one separately managed account; CBRE Caledon WR Holdings, LP / CBRE Infra Fiber LLC chain
company.description: Gateway Fiber is a CBRE Investment Management-owned U.S. fiber-broadband platform serving residential and business subscribers, schools, municipalities and institutional customers. The platform builds and operates fiber-to-the-home networks and lit-fiber, dark-fiber, E-Rate, special-construction and private-WAN infrastructure. Gateway Fiber was founded in 2019; CBRE first entered the combined predecessor group through its July 2021 acquisition of WANRack and acquired Gateway Fiber in 2023. WANRack acquired KwiKom in 2023. CBRE announced the Gateway Fiber-WANRack combination in February 2025, and Gateway Fiber confirmed by July 29, 2025 that the merger was complete and the combined business operated under the Gateway Fiber umbrella. WANRack, LLC remains an active legal and education-facing operating brand presented as WANRack Powered by Gateway Fiber, while KwiKom's consumer operations use the Gateway Fiber brand. WANRack reported 232 fiber WANs in 23 states and CBRE described the combined platform as serving communities or schools across approximately 25 states. Grain Management's former controlling WANRack interest ended at the 2021 CBRE closing. CBRE remains the current controlling sponsor; exact current economics and fund or SMA names are not publicly disclosed. The March 2025 Phoenix asset sale was a partial divestiture, and 2026 transfers to GW Operating were internal reorganizations with unchanged ultimate ownership. No later external platform sale or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 23, 2026.

company.description: Archived PortCo-census record for Alto, the brand used by VIA HFR–VIA TGF Inc. and its planned approximately 1,000-kilometre Toronto–Québec City high-speed rail network. VIA HFR–VIA TGF Inc. was incorporated on November 29, 2022 as a wholly owned subsidiary of VIA Rail Canada Inc. and operates as a federal agent Crown corporation. The Government of Canada selected the Cadence consortium as private developer in February 2025, and Alto and Cadence signed a project-development agreement in March 2025 to undertake route, design, environmental, land and financial-structure work. CDPQ Infra leads and holds equity in the separate Projet Cadence Rail developer vehicle; that interest does not constitute equity ownership of Alto. June 2026 market engagement remained part of early procurement before Canada's final investment decision. No CDPQ or CDPQ Infra acquisition of Alto shares or assets, closed concession, external sale or signed pending Alto ownership transfer was identified through August 23, 2026. The record is archived because Alto is a government-owned project entity rather than an infrastructure-fund portfolio company.

milestones.event: VIA HFR–VIA TGF Inc. was incorporated as VIA Rail Canada's wholly owned federal Crown subsidiary.
The Government of Canada announced the Alto high-speed rail program and selected Cadence as its private developer partner.
Alto and Cadence signed the project-development agreement and began co-development; the agreement did not transfer ownership of Alto to Cadence or CDPQ Infra.

company.name: Boralex Inc.
company.country: United States / Canada / France / United Kingdom
company.description: Boralex Inc. develops, builds, owns and operates wind, solar, hydroelectric and battery-storage assets across Canada, the United States, France and the United Kingdom. The company reported 3,822 MW of installed capacity and a nearly 8.2 GW development pipeline when its take-private closed on August 14, 2026. Boralex now operates as a private company owned 70% by Brookfield and 30% by La Caisse. Brookfield's interest is held through the Brookfield Infrastructure Fund V acquisition structure and BIF Thunder Holdings Inc., with Brookfield Renewable Partners among the participating partners. La Caisse first acquired 17.3% of Boralex on July 27, 2017, held approximately 15% before the take-private and continued or increased its equity to 30% at closing; no named La Caisse fund is publicly disclosed. A separate 2025 subordinated loan was debt and is not an ownership period. BIF Thunder is an acquisition vehicle rather than a separate PortCo. No later ownership transfer or signed pending sale was identified through August 23, 2026.

milestones.event: Boralex originated as a Québec joint venture; its renewable-power operating history began in 1990.
La Caisse acquired Cascades' 17.3% interest in Boralex, establishing its continuing equity position.
Brookfield and La Caisse completed the take-private, establishing current ownership at 70% and 30%, respectively.
Boralex shareholders approved the arrangement and the Québec Superior Court issued its final order.
Brookfield and La Caisse announced an all-cash agreement to take Boralex private for C$37.25 per share.

company.name: Renewa
company.description: Renewa LLC acquires land, lease interests, rental streams and royalties beneath operating and planned U.S. renewable-energy and power infrastructure, providing long-term site-control capital to landowners, developers, project owners, operators and independent power producers. EnCap founded the predecessor Paloma Solar & Wind in May 2021 and sold it to QIC-managed client capital in 2022; the platform adopted the Renewa name on September 20, 2022. La Caisse invested US$200 million of primary equity on July 15, 2025 through its Sustainable Land Management initiative. Renewa reported more than 160 facilities, more than 85 developers and over US$1.25 billion of capital commitments after a January 2026 financing. QIC manages a current ownership interest for undisclosed client or fund capital, and La Caisse is a current direct-equity owner; their percentages and exact legal vehicles are not publicly disclosed. Parcels, leases, financing SPVs and underlying projects remain assets rather than separate PortCos. No later platform sale, exit or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 23, 2026.

milestones.event: EnCap founded Paloma Solar & Wind, the predecessor of Renewa.
QIC acquired Paloma Solar & Wind for managed client capital; the platform adopted the Renewa name on September 20.
QIC-backed Renewa secured US$450 million of capital to expand its U.S. land-under-infrastructure portfolio.
La Caisse invested US$200 million of primary equity in QIC-backed Renewa through its Sustainable Land Management initiative.
Renewa secured US$502 million of financing, lifting total capital commitments above US$1.25 billion while remaining backed by QIC-managed funds and La Caisse.

company.name: TramCité
company.description: Archived PortCo-census record for TramCité, the planned approximately 19-kilometre, 29-station Québec City tramway. The Government of Québec is project owner, while Québec City and the Réseau de transport de la Capitale are the intended owners of the non-transport and transport assets, respectively. CDPQ Infra serves as maître d’œuvre under a State mandate, and its wholly owned subsidiary Infra CITÉ Inc. is a delivery and procurement mandatary rather than the asset owner. The implementation framework contemplates possible future CDPQ Infra capital or deferred financing, but the amount, return, repayment and risk allocation require government approval and a future definitive agreement. Procurement and co-development continued through July 2026. No direct CDPQ equity in TramCité, closed concession, definitive investment commitment, financial close, sale, transfer or signed pending private ownership transaction was identified through August 23, 2026. The record is archived because TramCité is a public project rather than an infrastructure-fund portfolio company.

milestones.event: Québec and CDPQ Infra signed the implementation framework, naming Québec as project owner and CDPQ Infra as maître d’œuvre without transferring project ownership.
The interface agreement identified Infra CITÉ as CDPQ Infra's wholly owned State mandatary and allocated future asset ownership to Québec City and the RTC.
TramCité selected preferred civil and systems consortia for a 14-month co-development phase; this procurement step was not a concession or ownership closing.

company.name: Vertical Bridge
company.description: Vertical Bridge REIT, LLC is a private U.S. wireless-infrastructure owner and operator providing build-to-suit and colocation capacity across towers, rooftops, utility structures, billboards and other communications sites. The company reports more than 500,000 sites, including more than 18,000 towers, serving wireless carriers and other communications tenants nationwide. DigitalBridge has invested since 2014 and completed a controlling-stake recapitalization in October 2021. La Caisse entered at a disclosed 30% stake in 2019; its current percentage is not publicly disclosed. KKR completed a US$1.5 billion equity investment through its core infrastructure strategy in 2026, while DigitalBridge and La Caisse remained investors; KKR's exact fund, affiliate and percentage are not public. InfraBridge is a DigitalBridge infrastructure-investment business unit rather than a direct owner. Towers, sites, portfolios and financing SPVs remain assets rather than separate PortCos. No later platform sale or current-sponsor exit was identified through August 23, 2026; SoftBank's announced acquisition of DigitalBridge is a manager-level transaction and not a direct transfer of Vertical Bridge.

milestones.event: Vertical Bridge was founded and DigitalBridge made its original investment.
La Caisse acquired a 30% interest in Vertical Bridge; the exact closing day and current post-2026 percentage are not publicly disclosed.
DigitalBridge completed its acquisition of a controlling stake in Vertical Bridge; The Jordan Company, GSAM infrastructure and Stonepeak exited.
Vertical Bridge closed its previously announced transaction for a Verizon tower portfolio, an asset acquisition rather than a change in platform ownership.
KKR completed a US$1.5 billion equity investment through its core infrastructure strategy; DigitalBridge and La Caisse remained investors, while exact post-financing percentages were not disclosed.
