company.name: Bolder Industries
company.description: Bolder Industries is a U.S. circular-materials infrastructure platform that converts end-of-life tires into recovered carbon black, pyrolysis oil, steel and energy for tire, rubber, plastics and other industrial customers. The company was founded in 2011 and is headquartered in Boulder, Colorado. Its operating and development footprint includes Maryville, Missouri, Terre Haute, Indiana and Antwerp, Belgium; those facilities and projects are not separate PortCos. CIM was an early investor and expanded its investment in October 2021. Tiger Infrastructure Partners completed a growth investment on February 10, 2025 through a recapitalization in which CIM participated, so Tiger joined rather than replaced CIM. Both sponsors remain current based on manager portfolio and board evidence. Their exact funds, vehicles, stakes and control rights, and CIM's original entry date, are not publicly disclosed. No later platform sale, exit, insolvency or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 23, 2026.

milestones.event: Bolder Industries was founded as a circular-materials company focused on recovering industrial products from end-of-life tires.
Bolder opened its Maryville, Missouri tire-recycling facility, an operating asset within the platform rather than a separate PortCo.
CIM expanded its existing Bolder investment as the company raised US$80 million of equity and secured US$100 million of committed project funding.

Tiger Infrastructure Partners completed a growth investment in Bolder through a recapitalization in which CIM participated; disclosed sources did not identify the funds, vehicles, stakes or control rights.
Tiger continued to list Bolder as a current investment and CIM retained board representation; no later ownership transfer or signed pending sale was found.

canonicalAfterImage.name: Bolder Industries
canonicalAfterImage.description: Bolder Industries is a U.S. circular-materials infrastructure platform that converts end-of-life tires into recovered carbon black, pyrolysis oil, steel and energy for tire, rubber, plastics and other industrial customers. The company was founded in 2011 and is headquartered in Boulder, Colorado. Its operating and development footprint includes Maryville, Missouri, Terre Haute, Indiana and Antwerp, Belgium; those facilities and projects are not separate PortCos. CIM was an early investor and expanded its investment in October 2021. Tiger Infrastructure Partners completed a growth investment on February 10, 2025 through a recapitalization in which CIM participated, so Tiger joined rather than replaced CIM. Both sponsors remain current based on manager portfolio and board evidence. Their exact funds, vehicles, stakes and control rights, and CIM's original entry date, are not publicly disclosed. No later platform sale, exit, insolvency or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 23, 2026.

company.name: Novva Data Centers
company.description: Novva Data Centers is a CIM Group-backed U.S. wholesale and colocation data-center platform serving hyperscale, cloud, artificial-intelligence and enterprise customers across the western United States. The company was founded in 2020 with funding from CIM and Novva's founders, received an additional US$355 million of CIM growth equity in 2022 and announced US$2 billion of new financing with CIM in 2025. Novva announced on November 29, 2023 that it had acquired the 400 Paul Avenue campus in San Francisco and now markets the site as Novva Data Centers–San Francisco. The campus had been acquired by a CIM/1547 joint venture in August 2017, entered construction in April 2018 and was marketed at approximately 24 MW before Novva's acquisition; Novva currently markets 36 MW on the 7.5-acre site. The seller, exact Novva closing date, retained CIM/1547 site economics and independently verified commissioned capacity are not publicly disclosed. CIM remains the current manager-level sponsor of Novva; its fund, vehicle and ownership percentage are not public. 400 Paul is an underlying facility and alias rather than a separate PortCo. No later sale or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 23, 2026.

company.ownershipVehicle: CIM Real Assets & Credit Fund and another CIM-managed institutional fund; IENTC 1, LLC for RACR
company.description: IENTC Telecomunicaciones is a Mexican telecommunications operator that owns and operates fiber infrastructure serving carrier, corporate and residential customers. The company provides dedicated internet access, data transport, dark fiber, fiber-to-the-home and telephony services and reports approximately 37,500 kilometres of fiber across Mexico. Its legal name is IENTC, S. de R.L. de C.V., and it is headquartered in Santiago de Querétaro. CIM-managed funds invested in the first quarter of 2022 and retain 45% aggregate equity with board representation; CIM Real Assets & Credit Fund separately reported a 21.3% interest in IENTC 1, LLC. IENTC 2 debt was repaid in full during fiscal 2025, but the equity investment remained active. The exact legal chain between IENTC 1 and the Mexican operating company, the second CIM vehicle and the non-CIM shareholder identities are not publicly disclosed. IENTC is unrelated to the separate Sempra company Infraestructura Energética Nova. No CIM equity exit or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 19, 2026.

company.name: SolarBank Joint Venture (New HoldCo)
company.description: Archived PortCo-census record for a contemplated SolarBank/PowerBank and CIM financing structure announced on May 6, 2025. The original non-binding mandate contemplated a newly formed holding company that could acquire interests in 21 U.S. renewable projects totaling approximately 97 MW and issue preferred equity to CIM, subject to definitive documents, project-level conditions and funding. PowerBank later disclosed that negotiations had been refocused toward a proposed secured development loan to its subsidiary Abundant Solar Power for 14 New York projects totaling approximately 48 MWdc, while the documents remained unexecuted. No legal name, jurisdiction, formation, project transfer, CIM equity investment, CIM loan funding, operating assets, employees, definitive closing or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 19, 2026. The record is archived because the proposed New HoldCo never became a verified operating company or direct CIM portfolio company; PowerBank, ASP and the underlying projects remain outside this placeholder record.

milestones.event: SolarBank and CIM announced a non-binding mandate for up to US$100 million; the contemplated New HoldCo, preferred equity and project transfers required future definitive documents and conditions.

PowerBank's annual MD&A reported that definitive CIM documentation remained unexecuted and that no funding would occur without completed agreements.

PowerBank reported that negotiations had shifted from preferred equity/New HoldCo to a proposed secured development loan to ASP for 14 New York projects totaling approximately 48 MWdc; documents remained unexecuted.
A subsequent-event and exit search found no New HoldCo formation, project transfer, CIM funding, definitive closing or signed pending ownership transaction.

company.name: Permanent Power Company
company.subsector: Utility-scale solar, battery storage and transmission
company.ownershipVehicle: CIM Opportunity Zone Fund, L.P. (direct and through COZ 1, LLC)
company.description: Permanent Power Company is a CIM Group-backed U.S. power-infrastructure platform that owns and develops utility-scale solar generation, battery storage and transmission assets. SEC filings identify Permanent Power Company, LLC as the renamed former Westlands Electric Power Company, LLC. At March 31, 2026, CIM Opportunity Zone Fund held approximately 66.7% of the company, including its direct interest and the interest held through COZ 1, while other CIM-affiliated entities held the remaining 33.3%. CIM launched the Permanent Power brand in May 2026 with 652 MW of operating solar, 360 MW/1,440 MWh of battery storage and 15 miles of transmission, plus the Grape and Daylight projects in construction or construction-ready development. Westlands Solar Park is the California site/master plan beneath Permanent Power, and Aquamarine is its first 250 MW utility-scale solar project rather than a separate portfolio company. The Westlands development lineage began in 2014, construction started in 2020 and Aquamarine entered commercial operation in late 2021. The exact rename effective date, company headquarters and identities within the 33.3% CIM-affiliate block are not publicly disclosed. No third-party sale, change of control or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 19, 2026.

canonicalAfterImage.subsector: Utility-scale solar, battery storage and transmission
canonicalAfterImage.description: Permanent Power Company is a CIM Group-backed U.S. power-infrastructure platform that owns and develops utility-scale solar generation, battery storage and transmission assets. SEC filings identify Permanent Power Company, LLC as the renamed former Westlands Electric Power Company, LLC. At March 31, 2026, CIM Opportunity Zone Fund held approximately 66.7% of the company, including its direct interest and the interest held through COZ 1, while other CIM-affiliated entities held the remaining 33.3%. CIM launched the Permanent Power brand in May 2026 with 652 MW of operating solar, 360 MW/1,440 MWh of battery storage and 15 miles of transmission, plus the Grape and Daylight projects in construction or construction-ready development. Westlands Solar Park is the California site/master plan beneath Permanent Power, and Aquamarine is its first 250 MW utility-scale solar project rather than a separate portfolio company. The Westlands development lineage began in 2014, construction started in 2020 and Aquamarine entered commercial operation in late 2021. The exact rename effective date, company headquarters and identities within the 33.3% CIM-affiliate block are not publicly disclosed. No third-party sale, change of control or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 19, 2026.

company.name: Horizon New Energy
company.description: Horizon New Energy is Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners' Canadian renewable-development platform. CIP launched Horizon in November 2023 with approximately 1.2 GW of Alberta solar, wind and battery-storage projects. Horizon lists the 450 MWac Aira Solar development near Seven Persons, Alberta as one of its projects; Aira is therefore an underlying project and associated SPVs rather than a second manager-level PortCo. Alberta registry records identify CI V Horizon New Energy Devco Ltd and CI V Aira entities, including a March 2025 internal amalgamation into CI V Aira Holdco Ltd. The project has received AESO connection and Alberta Utilities Commission approvals and remained active in AESO's August 2026 project list, but a final investment decision, financing close, construction start, offtaker and commercial-operation date were not publicly disclosed. No third-party platform sale, Aira transfer or signed pending exit was identified through August 19, 2026.

company.name: Vineyard Offshore
company.description: Vineyard Offshore is Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners' U.S. offshore-wind development platform, established in 2022 with lease areas held through CI IV. Excelsior Wind is the current 1,350 MW New York project configuration within the broader Vineyard Mid-Atlantic federal lease and construction-and-operations-plan envelope, whose legal lessee is Vineyard Mid-Atlantic LLC. Excelsior is therefore a nested project and lease SPV history, not a second manager-level PortCo. The lease became effective in May 2022; New York provisionally selected an earlier 1,314 MW configuration in 2023, but no final award or executed offtake followed, and the later 1,350 MW bid received no award when the 2024 solicitation closed in February 2026. BOEM began environmental review in January 2025, and the project remains in development and uncontracted. No lease transfer, sale, relinquishment, CIP exit or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 19, 2026.

milestones.event: Public platform materials state that Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners-supported Vineyard Offshore was established in 2022 with initial lease areas owned by Copenhagen Infrastructure IV (CI IV).
Vineyard Offshore was founded.
Vineyard Offshore announced New York's provisional selection of an earlier Excelsior Wind configuration, but the round closed without a final award or executed offtake.
Vineyard Offshore announced Vineyard Northeast for New England.
Federal lease OCS-A 0544 became effective for Vineyard Mid-Atlantic LLC, the lease SPV for the area containing Excelsior Wind.
BOEM issued its notice of intent to prepare an environmental impact statement for the broader Vineyard Mid-Atlantic project.
NYSERDA closed the 2024 offshore-wind solicitation without awards, leaving Excelsior's 1,350 MW bid uncontracted.

company.description: Helax Istmo is a Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners-owned development company for a large renewable-energy and industrial project in Oaxaca, Mexico. CIP's December 2023 disclosure identifies Helax as wholly owned collectively by CI Growth Markets Fund II and Copenhagen Infrastructure Energy Transition Fund I and describes a memorandum of understanding with Mexican authorities for an originally proposed renewable-power, green-hydrogen and green-maritime-fuels development. The individual fund split, entry date and committed project equity were not disclosed. CIP later said the project structure and scope remained under review, while public reporting indicated a possible redesign toward electricity generation. No current concession, final permit, offtake agreement, final investment decision, financing close, construction start or operating asset was verified. Helax remains one pre-development PortCo; CIIT, SEMAR, the Ciudad Ixtepec industrial site and any project facilities are counterparties or assets rather than separate owners. No sale, partner entry, exit or signed pending ownership transaction was found through August 19, 2026.

company.name: Sunrise Renewables
company.description: Sunrise Renewables is a staffed Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners development platform for utility-scale solar and battery-storage projects in the United States. Kentucky regulatory filings identify the legal vehicle as CI V Sunrise Renewables LLC, held through CI V Sunrise HoldCo LLC, and place the Lost City project SPV beneath that chain. The filings also identify Sunrise personnel working across Lost City Solar in Kentucky and disclosed solar and battery developments in South Carolina. Sunrise is therefore retained as the manager-level CI V platform, while Lost City, Gullah Geechee Renewable Energy Center Solar, Cypress Gardens BESS and their SPVs remain underlying projects. Public evidence does not support the prior CI IV ownership, a green-hydrogen scope, a Kentucky headquarters or a 2022 CIP entry date. A New York business address appears in filings, but the formal headquarters is not publicly disclosed. company.name: Vineyard Offshore
company.description: Vineyard Offshore is Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners' U.S. offshore-wind development platform, established in 2022 with federal lease interests held through CI IV. Its disclosed portfolio includes Excelsior Wind within OCS-A 0544 and Vineyard Northeast within OCS-A 0522, as well as other east- and west-coast developments. Vineyard Northeast is the lease and project identity for OCS-A 0522, whose current lessee is Vineyard Northeast LLC; Vineyard Wind 2 is a proposed project of up to 1.2 GW inside that lease, not a separate manager-level company. A 50/50 Avangrid and CIP joint venture won the lease in 2018 and it became effective on April 1, 2019. On January 10, 2022, a CI IV vehicle acquired Avangrid's interest and obtained 100% of the lease rights. Massachusetts provisionally selected 800 MW in September 2024, but Vineyard Offshore withdrew the bid on December 20, 2024 after Connecticut made no offshore-wind selection. The lease remains active, while FAST-41 permitting is paused to April 1, 2027; no PPA, FID, financing close, construction start, lease surrender, sale, CIP exit or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 19, 2026. Vineyard Northeast, Vineyard Wind 2, Excelsior Wind and their lease SPVs are consolidated beneath this one platform record; Vineyard Wind 1 remains distinct.

company.ownershipVehicle: Promotora Punta Cometa, S.A. de C.V.
company.description: Autopista Arco Norte, S.A. de C.V., commonly known as Arco Norte, operates a 223-kilometer federal user-pay toll road across the State of Mexico, Hidalgo, Tlaxcala and Puebla. The concession was granted on December 21, 2005 and is scheduled to expire on December 20, 2065. IDEAL contributed its 99% Arco Norte interest to Promotora Punta Cometa, S.A. de C.V. in the partnership that closed on December 22, 2016; at close, CPP Investments held 29% of that vehicle and Ontario Teachers' held 20%, alongside IDEAL and a small Inbursa affiliate interest. Later FIDEAL restructuring changed the direct capitalization beneath the road, so current manager look-through percentages are not publicly disclosed and the 2016 percentages should not be presented as direct concessionaire stakes. Ontario Teachers' continues to list Arco Norte separately from IDEAL, supporting treatment as its own manager-level infrastructure holding. No manager exit, concession transfer, termination or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 19, 2026. Promotora Punta Cometa is the upstream holding vehicle; IDEAL Group and Pacifico Sur remain separate investments.

company.ownershipVehicle: Kimmeridge-managed funds; exact allocation not publicly disclosed
company.description: Caturus is an integrated U.S. natural-gas and LNG platform whose legal parent is Caturus Holdco, LLC, renamed from SoTex HoldCo in August 2025. The platform combines Caturus Energy's Texas upstream production with the controlled 9.5 mtpa Commonwealth LNG export project in Cameron Parish, Louisiana. After the May 14, 2026 CPP Investments closing, regulatory filings support a direct governance cap table of 52.6% Kimmeridge-managed interests, 24.1% Mubadala, 22.8% CPP Investments and 0.5% Caturus management. CPP also has a disclosed economic look-through through Kimmeridge-managed funds, but that indirect interest carries no additional governance and public CPP percentages use a different aggregation basis; the 22.8% direct interest is therefore used for the ownership row. Kimmeridge's exact fund allocation and CPP's primary-versus-secondary mix are not publicly disclosed. Caturus reported more than 1 Bcfe per day of net production across approximately 280,000 net acres after the Galvan Ranch acquisition, while Commonwealth LNG reached FID and closed project financing in May 2026. Caturus Energy and Commonwealth LNG are subordinate operating subsidiaries/projects, not separate manager-level PortCos, and project financiers are not parent owners. No later platform sale, owner exit, cancellation or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 19, 2026.

company.name: Cordelio Power
company.description: Cordelio Power was a Toronto-headquartered wind, solar and energy-storage platform operating in Canada and the United States. CPP Investments wholly owned the business from its June 29, 2018 entry until Pattern Energy's share-based acquisition closed on April 1, 2026. Pattern acquired approximately 1,550 MW across 16 operating or construction projects, most of Cordelio's U.S. development portfolio and the Cordelio team; Cordelio is therefore retained as a historical acquired company subordinate to Pattern, not as a separate active CPP Investments PortCo. CPP's continuing exposure is represented through its 69.1% ownership of Pattern. BrightNight separately announced on April 21, 2026 that it had acquired Cordelio's interest in a 6 GW development joint venture, a partial asset-level divestiture rather than a second company-level exit. Public sources reviewed do not establish the exact surviving merger entity, so dissolution is not inferred.

company.name: Pacifico Sur
company.description: Pacifico Sur is the operating toll-road concession held through Concesionaria Autopista Guadalajara Tepic, S.A. de C.V. (CAGT). Its 309.6-kilometer network in Jalisco and Nayarit includes the Guadalajara–Tepic toll road, the South Guadalajara Bypass and the Tepic Bypass, serving freight, tourism and other toll-paying road users under a long-duration user-pay concession. A definitive agreement was announced on October 2, 2018 and the direct purchase of 49% of CAGT closed on May 15, 2019, leaving IDEAL with 51%, CPP Investments with 29% and Ontario Teachers' with 20%. A 2020 modification extended the concession to 60 years from November 30, 2011, implying expiry in November 2071. Pacifico Sur remains a separate direct PortCo from IDEAL Group and Autopista Arco Norte, and no later direct-stake sale, concession transfer or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 19, 2026.

milestones.event: IDEAL, CPP Investments and Ontario Teachers' announced the direct CAGT share purchase at 51%, 29% and 20%, respectively.
The purchase of 49% of CAGT closed, establishing CPP Investments' 29% and Ontario Teachers' 20% direct interests alongside IDEAL's 51% stake.
A concession modification extended Pacifico Sur's term to 60 years from November 30, 2011.
Ontario Teachers' continued to list Pacifico Sur separately from IDEAL Group and Arco Norte.

company.name: TransAlta Keephills Data Centre JV
company.description: Archived proposed data-centre development at TransAlta's Keephills site in Parkland County, Alberta. TransAlta signed a memorandum of understanding on February 26, 2026 with CPP Investments and Brookfield as prospective proponents or customers for an initial approximately 230 MW phase with potential to scale to 1 GW. Direct sources state that the proposal remained subject to regulatory approvals and future definitive binding agreements; no separate JV or SPV, CPP equity stake, investment vehicle, committed capital, definitive joint-venture agreement, PPA or lease, financial close or legal investment close was verified through August 19, 2026. AESO grid-connection activity is project-development evidence, not manager ownership. The row is therefore excluded from the active PortCo census and carries no ownership period or pending ownership transaction; it may be reassessed only after a verifiable definitive equity agreement and close.

company.name: American Student Transportation Partners (ASTP)
company.description: American Student Transportation Partners (ASTP) provides contracted K-12 student transportation through traditional school-bus routes and alternative and special-needs transportation. It serves school districts through route-based operations supported by vehicles, depots, drivers and local operating systems. At the August 2025 transaction announcement, ASTP transported more than 90,000 students annually for more than 50 districts with more than 2,300 vehicles. CVC DIF agreed to acquire the platform from Access Holdings through DIF Infrastructure VII on August 12, 2025, and Access described the sale as a successful exit by September 15, 2025. The exact legal close date, stake and acquisition vehicle below the fund are not publicly disclosed. Krise Transportation and Assisted Student Transportation are operating companies beneath ASTP, and Brandywine routes and vehicles are acquired assets rather than separate manager-level PortCos. No later platform sale or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 19, 2026.

CVC DIF agreed to acquire ASTP from Access Holdings through DIF Infrastructure VII.
Access Holdings described ASTP's sale to CVC DIF as a successful exit, confirming the transaction had completed by that date.
ASTP continued operating through Krise and Assisted across Pennsylvania, Kansas and Missouri.
CVC DIF reported that ASTP served more than 90,000 students annually across more than 50 districts with more than 2,300 vehicles.
Access Holdings completed its exit from ASTP to CVC DIF; the exact legal closing date was not publicly disclosed.

company.name: CARMA Corp.
company.description: CARMA Corp. provides utility submetering, billing, collections, consumption reporting and on-site technical services for multi-residential, commercial and institutional properties. The company traces its predecessor operations to 1977 and was formed as CARMA Corp. through the August 2019 amalgamation of Carma Industries Inc. and Carma Billing Services Inc. CVC DIF agreed to acquire CARMA from TerraNova through DIF Infrastructure VIII on September 15, 2025, and industry-association reporting confirms the sale closed in December 2025. The disclosed acquisition vehicle is DIF Infra 8 Canada Holdco 2 Ltd.; the exact closing day, acquired stake and any management or family rollover are not publicly disclosed. CARMA operated more than 135,000 units across more than 1,000 buildings at signing and was reported to have approximately 350,000 meters installed across North America by June 2026. Spectrum, Priority Submetering, Undercurrent and Greensource remain operating businesses beneath CARMA rather than separate manager-level PortCos. No later sale or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 19, 2026.

milestones.event: TerraNova and Michael Platt acquired majority control in partnership with the Williams family, and CARMA's predecessor entities amalgamated into CARMA Corp.

The sale closed, making CVC DIF through DIF Infrastructure VIII the current owner and ending TerraNova's holding period.

company.name: ENFRA
company.subsector: Energy solutions and building infrastructure services
company.description: ENFRA, LLC designs, builds, finances and operates energy, engineering and building-infrastructure solutions for healthcare, higher-education, government, commercial and industrial customers. The company provides engineering, construction, commissioning, maintenance, asset management, optimization, resilience and energy-as-a-service solutions. ENFRA is the same continuing legal entity formerly named Bernhard, LLC; the legal name changed effective May 1, 2025 without changing the entity, EIN, ownership, legal structure or contracts. DIF Infrastructure VI agreed to acquire Bernhard in October 2021 and the sale closed on December 2, 2021. ENFRA continues to identify CVC DIF as its majority owner; the exact fund stake, management rollover percentage and acquisition SPV are not publicly disclosed. The company traces its predecessor heritage to 1919, is headquartered in Metairie, Louisiana and reports operations across 18 states. Subsidiaries, tuck-ins and customer energy-as-a-service projects remain beneath ENFRA unless separate manager ownership is proven. No later sale or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 19, 2026.

company.name: JW Water Holdings, LLC
company.description: JW Water Holdings, LLC is a regulated water and wastewater utility platform serving more than 50,000 customers in Arizona. CVC DIF completed the acquisition of JW Water's ten-utility platform and eight Robson utilities through DIF Infrastructure VII in November 2024. Pima became a wholly owned JW Water subsidiary on November 20, 2024, and current company and Arizona Corporation Commission materials show the acquired utilities operating beneath the integrated JW Water platform. Public sources do not disclose CVC DIF's exact ownership percentage or a separate acquisition SPV. Later Pima and other utility consolidations are internal legal and regulatory reorganizations, not manager-level ownership transfers. No later sale, sponsor exit or signed pending manager-level transaction was identified through August 19, 2026.

milestones.event: Public utility materials state that Pima Utility began serving Arizona communities in 1972; Pima is retained here as a child-utility history item within JW Water.
JW Water Holdings was founded.

CVC DIF stated that the combined Arizona utility platform would serve more than 50,000 customers; current JW materials present the integrated business as 18 legacy utility brands and 20 water and wastewater systems.
Pima Utility became a wholly owned subsidiary of JW Water Holdings, confirming that Pima is an underlying utility rather than a separate manager-level PortCo.
CVC DIF acquired JW Water and the eight-utility Robson portfolio through DIF Infrastructure VII, consolidating them as one manager-level Arizona utility platform.

The Arizona Corporation Commission approved an internal consolidation of Bensch Ranch, Pine Meadows and Verde Santa Fe utilities and identified JW Water Holdings as owner of those utilities and 15 others.
The Arizona Corporation Commission approved the internal consolidation of Quail Creek, Ridgeview and Lago Del Oro into JW Water Utility Company.

company.description: ValorC3 Data Centers is the operating name of Tonaquint Data Centers, LLC, a regional U.S. data-center platform providing colocation, private cloud, connectivity, disaster recovery, backup and build-to-suit capacity. The platform serves enterprise, channel and hyperscale customers from St. George, Utah, Boise, Idaho and Oklahoma City, Oklahoma. CVC DIF acquired a majority interest through DIF CIF III in December 2022; management retained a minority interest, while exact percentages and the legal closing day were not publicly disclosed. Tonaquint acquired EdgeX in November 2023 and began operating as ValorC3 on January 20, 2025 without creating a new company. Current materials report 19 MW of operating capacity plus a 10 MW Boise facility under development and a second 10 MW facility planned. A 2026 company financing announcement still identified CVC DIF as sponsor, and no later sale, transfer or signed pending exit was identified through August 19, 2026.

company.name: Beanfield Metroconnect
company.subsector: Metro fiber broadband and enterprise connectivity
company.description: Beanfield Metroconnect, legally Beanfield Technologies Inc., builds, owns and operates metropolitan fibre networks and provides residential broadband, business connectivity, private networks, cloud connectivity and colocation services in Canada. The platform serves residential and multi-dwelling-unit customers, enterprises, carriers and data centres across Toronto, Montreal, Ottawa and Vancouver, with additional points of presence in Calgary, New York and Seattle. Public transaction materials reported approximately 4,000 kilometres of fibre connecting roughly 4,000 commercial buildings and more than 170,000 residential units in 2023; current scale was not publicly disclosed. Digital Colony Partners acquired Beanfield in November 2019. OMERS Infrastructure completed a minority investment on September 15, 2023, after which DigitalBridge remained the majority owner. OpenFace was integrated into Beanfield, and Beanfield acquired Aptum's metro-network assets rather than Aptum itself. Current DigitalBridge and OMERS materials continue to list Beanfield, and no Beanfield-specific sale, ownership transfer or signed pending exit was identified through August 19, 2026.

milestones.event: Beanfield was founded in Toronto.

Beanfield announced a C$255 million recapitalization following the OpenFace integration and the acquisition of Aptum's Toronto and Montreal metro-network assets.
Beanfield acquired OpenFace and integrated its Montreal fibre operations into the Beanfield platform.
OMERS Infrastructure announced a minority investment in Beanfield while DigitalBridge said it would remain the majority owner.
OMERS Infrastructure completed its minority investment in Beanfield Technologies Inc., with DigitalBridge continuing as majority owner.

company.name: Fibernow
company.description: Fibernow, formerly branded OpticalTel and legally associated with Optical Telecommunications, Inc., provides fiber internet, managed Wi-Fi and IT, streaming television and digital voice services to communities, homeowners associations, businesses, student housing and assisted-living or hospitality customers. The verified operating footprint is centered in Florida; broader current scale is not publicly disclosed. DigitalBridge Partners III invested through DBP III Snowbird BidCo on February 29, 2024, and OpticalTel publicly rebranded as Fibernow in October 2024. Fibernow acquired and integrated Wavetechs in the first quarter of 2025. InfraBridge is not a direct owner, and no company-level sale or signed pending exit was identified through August 19, 2026.

company.name: Invenergy AMPCI Thermal Power
company.ownershipVehicle: AMP Capital Global Infrastructure Fund II (GIF II)
company.description: Invenergy AMPCI Thermal Power LLC is a 50/50 joint venture that owns a portfolio of dispatchable power-generation assets across the United States and Canada. InfraBridge holds one half through the legacy AMP Capital Global Infrastructure Fund II strategy, and Invenergy Clean Power holds the other half and continues to operate and manage the portfolio. Public materials report 11 facilities totaling approximately 5.4 GW gross and 3.2 GW net. On March 12, 2026, ArcLight signed an agreement to acquire InfraBridge's 50% interest through disclosed Gray Wolf acquisition vehicles. Regulatory reviews advanced, but no FERC approval, consummation notice or party closing release was identified through August 19, 2026; InfraBridge therefore remains the current legal owner and ArcLight remains a pending incoming buyer.

milestones.event: Invenergy and AMP Capital announced a 50/50 partnership for the North American thermal-power portfolio, with Invenergy retaining management responsibility.
The 50/50 Invenergy and legacy GIF II investment in Invenergy AMPCI Thermal Power commenced; the exact closing day was not publicly disclosed.
ArcLight signed an agreement to acquire InfraBridge's 50% interest, while Invenergy remained the continuing 50% owner and operator.
The parties filed the pending ArcLight acquisition with FERC under docket EC26-76.
U.S. antitrust and Canadian merger reviews advanced, but those clearances did not establish a legal closing of the ArcLight acquisition.

company.name: Mexico Telecom Partners
company.subsector: Wireless towers and edge digital infrastructure
company.description: Mexico Telecom Partners, legally Mexico Tower Partners, S.A.P.I. de C.V., is a neutral Mexican digital-infrastructure platform that owns and operates towers, rooftop sites, distributed antenna systems, small cells, edge facilities and data-center infrastructure. The platform serves major wireless operators and colocation users across Mexico. It was formed in May 2014 by combining Digital Bridge and Macquarie Mexican Infrastructure Fund portfolios. A June 2026 BMV filing reported approximately 3,737 sites and confirmed an unchanged 50/50 ownership split: DigitalBridge through MTP Mexico Holding B.V., and Macquarie Asset Management through MMIT I and MMIT II. The 2022 Macquarie-side transfer was internal, InfraBridge is not a direct owner, and no signed or closed direct platform sale was identified through August 19, 2026.

milestones.event: The 50/50 Digital Bridge and Macquarie Mexican Infrastructure Fund combination closed to form Mexico Tower Partners; the transaction was announced the following day.
Macquarie transferred its MTP shares and related loans internally to MMIT I and MMIT II without changing Macquarie's aggregate 50% interest.

company.name: Switch, Inc.
company.description: Switch, Inc. develops, owns and operates large-scale U.S. data-center campuses serving AI, cloud and enterprise customers. The platform was founded in 2000 and is headquartered in Las Vegas, with campuses in Nevada, Texas, Michigan and Georgia and a Pennsylvania expansion announced in 2026. DigitalBridge Partners II and IFM Global Infrastructure Fund completed the take-private on December 6, 2022. company.name: WideOpenWest, Inc.
company.description: WideOpenWest, Inc. (WOW!) is a U.S. broadband network operator providing high-speed internet, video, voice, mobile, business data and related connectivity services to residential, commercial and wholesale customers. The company operates across 19 markets in Michigan, Alabama, Tennessee, South Carolina, Georgia and Florida and reports nearly two million network passings. Operations began in 2001; the current corporation was formed in 2012 and adopted the WideOpenWest name in 2017. Crestview first invested in December 2015. DigitalBridge and Crestview completed a $1.5 billion take-private on December 31, 2025 through Bandit Parent and its subsidiaries; DigitalBridge Partners III holds approximately 63% and Crestview III approximately 37% of Bandit Parent's limited-partner interests, with equal general-partner control. InfraBridge is not a direct owner. SoftBank's signed acquisition of DigitalBridge remains an upstream manager transaction and was not treated as a direct WOW ownership transfer through August 19, 2026.

company.name: Mantle Reach Power
company.description: Mantle Reach Power LLC is a geothermal independent power producer that develops, finances, owns and operates generation projects intended to provide firm, around-the-clock carbon-free power across North America. Target end markets include electric utilities, industrial users and large loads such as AI and hyperscale data centers. The company is backed by EnCap Energy Transition Fund III and in June 2026 announced a Baker Hughes agreement targeting up to 500 MW over five years; current commissioned, operating and development capacity is not publicly disclosed. EnCap reports a 2023 initial investment under the Mantle Reach name, but public evidence does not establish the original fund, vehicle or legal continuity into the current 2026 geothermal LLC, so no entry year or stake is inferred for the active Fund III ownership period. No sale, exit or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 19, 2026.

company.name: Anza Renewables
company.ownershipVehicle: ECP Energy Transition Opportunities Fund-led consortium
company.description: Anza Renewables is the operating brand of Anza RE, LLC, a U.S. software-enabled procurement, data and analytics platform serving solar and battery-storage developers, independent power producers and other energy buyers. Its tools support module, inverter, storage and transformer sourcing, supplier evaluation and purchase-order execution. The business formally launched from Borrego in September 2022. Borrego contracted to sell all Anza RE, LLC equity to Anza RE Buyer, LLC on February 24, 2023 for US$26.74 million, and Anza announced the completed separation on May 17, 2023 with investment from ECP's Energy Transition Opportunities Fund, Angeleno Group and other investors. ECP and Angeleno continue to list Anza as active; exact stakes, control, the full cap table and the legal closing day are not publicly disclosed. The company is headquartered in Oakland, California and reports more than 80 subscribers and support for over 8 GW of PV and 5 GWh of BESS purchase orders. No later sale or signed pending exit was identified through August 19, 2026.

Operating through the Avolta Development brand, the company develops, finances, owns and operates dairy and landfill RNG projects, including feedstock and site rights, digesters, gas-upgrading equipment, pipeline interconnections, offtake and environmental-credit arrangements. End markets include pipeline gas utilities, transportation-fuel programs and other low-carbon fuel buyers. ECP continues to list the platform as current, and Avolta published current Texas operating activity in May 2026. Exact ownership percentages, governance economics, ECP fund and legal holding vehicle are not publicly disclosed. Avolta, LLC is headquartered in Charleston, West Virginia; Texas, Florida and Arizona are operating or project locations rather than headquarters. company.ownershipVehicle: Preferred-equity investment; exact investing vehicle not publicly disclosed
company.description: Braya Renewable Fuels is the manager-level renewable-fuels platform operating the Come By Chance refinery in Newfoundland and Labrador through Braya Renewable Fuels (Newfoundland) LP. Cresta Fund Management acquired control in November 2021, while Silverpeak-managed North Atlantic Refining Corp. retained a minority interest. ECP announced a US$300 million preferred-equity investment in April 2023. Exact sponsor percentages, voting rights and holding vehicles are not publicly disclosed, and ECP Fund V is not directly supported for this investment. Commercial renewable-diesel operations began in February 2024; after a temporary 2025 shutdown, operations resumed, and the platform announced its first 100,000-barrel Canadian renewable-diesel sale in June 2026. Braya serves fuel markets in Canada, the United States, Mexico and Europe, while sustainable aviation fuel and green hydrogen or ammonia remain planned rather than confirmed commercial products. No later sale, sponsor exit or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 19, 2026.

company.name: Gopher Resource
company.ownershipVehicle: Energy Capital Partners IV-A, LP; immediate parent ECP Gopher Holdings, LP
company.description: Gopher Resource is the operating name of Gopher Resource, LLC, a U.S. lead-battery recycling platform founded in 1946 and headquartered in Eagan, Minnesota. ECP's Energy Capital Partners IV-A, LP acquired the company in a transaction announced January 30 and closed March 6, 2018. A 2025 federal disclosure identifies ECP Gopher Holdings, LP as the sole immediate parent; the ECP economic interest, purchase price, rollover and co-investors are not publicly disclosed. Gopher operates recycling plants in Eagan and Tampa under mostly fixed, multi-year fee-for-service arrangements and reported processing more than 24 million batteries annually, employing more than 625 people, and recovering more than 41 million pounds of plastic and approximately 600 million pounds of lead in 2025. EnviroFocus, Resource Plastics, the facilities and The Recycling Zone remain subsidiaries, assets or operated sites rather than separate PortCos. A 2020 internal ECP HSR notice and the October 2024 US$450 million refinancing do not establish an outside-party exit, and no later sale or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 19, 2026.

Gopher closed a US$450 million refinancing supported by additional ECP equity; the transaction did not transfer platform ownership.
Gopher reported that its 2025 operations recovered more than 41 million pounds of plastic and approximately 600 million pounds of lead.

company.name: Harvestone Low Carbon Partners
company.description: Harvestone Low Carbon Partners, LP is a U.S. low-carbon fuels and carbon-management platform formed in 2022 by ECP and Harvestone Group. ECP attributes the investment to ECP Fund V, and both partners continue to identify the platform as active; exact stakes, control and holding vehicles are not publicly disclosed. Through HLCP Ethanol Holdco, the platform acquired Midwest AgEnergy, including Blue Flint and Dakota Spirit and its 40% Coal Creek interest, and also acquired Iroquois Bio-Energy. Those facilities, subsidiaries and project entities remain subordinate to the manager-level platform. The three dry-mill biorefineries produce approximately 215 million gallons of ethanol, 490,000 tons of distillers grains and 9.6 million gallons of corn oil annually, while Blue Flint stores approximately 220,000 metric tons of carbon dioxide. Bank of America's September 2024 US$205 million Blue Flint CCS tax-equity investment is project financing rather than platform ownership. No later platform sale, sponsor exit or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 19, 2026.

milestones.event: ECP and Harvestone Group formed Harvestone Low Carbon Partners; HLCP Ethanol Holdco closed the acquisition of Midwest AgEnergy, including Blue Flint and Dakota Spirit, and the platform also acquired IBEC.
Harvestone and Bank of America closed US$205 million of tax-equity financing for the Blue Flint carbon-capture project; the financing did not transfer platform ownership.

company.name: New Leaf Energy
company.ownershipVehicle: Zorro DevCo Parent, Inc. / Zorro DevCo Merger Sub, Inc.; exact current holding vehicle not publicly disclosed
company.description: New Leaf Energy, Inc. is a U.S. solar and energy-storage development platform formed in 2022 through the carve-out of Borrego's development business. It originates and advances commercial, community and utility-scale projects through siting, interconnection, permitting, offtake and construction-ready handoff. ECP completed its acquisition on July 27, 2022 and continues to list New Leaf as current; its exact current stake, fund and holding vehicle are not publicly disclosed. Walsin Lihwa's controlling block was sold in the 2022 transaction, and Walsin America separately sold back its entire 88,729-share block to New Leaf, leaving Walsin with no current interest. Borrego's retained EPC/O&M/Anza businesses and individual project companies or portfolios remain outside the canonical platform. ECP reports a pipeline of approximately 15 GW of solar and 7 GW of storage, with about 1 GW of photovoltaic projects and 450 MWh of battery projects sold. No later platform sale, sponsor exit or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 29, 2026.

ECP legally completed the acquisition and New Leaf began operating as the standalone development platform; public completion was announced July 28.

company.description: Next Wave Energy Partners, LP is a Houston-based downstream and midstream infrastructure platform that develops, owns and operates toll-processing, manufacturing and logistics assets for natural gas liquids, petrochemicals and gasoline blend components. ECP first invested alongside management in 2015 with an equity commitment of up to US$500 million; ECP reports a March 2018 investment date and later identifies Next Wave as a Fund IV investment. Those disclosures establish continuous ECP ownership but do not disclose the Fund IV transition mechanics, acquisition vehicle or stake. Project Traveler is the platform's Pasadena, Texas alkylate facility, and Pasadena Performance Products is its project subsidiary rather than a separate PortCo. The 53-acre facility was originally designed for 28,000 barrels per day and reached commercial operation December 28, 2023. No later platform or asset sale, ECP exit or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 19, 2026.

company.name: PROENERGY
company.subsector: Fast-start gas generation equipment, services, and contracted power
company.description: PROENERGY is a Sedalia, Missouri-based power-infrastructure platform founded in 2002 that manufactures and packages aeroderivative generation equipment, executes turnkey projects, supplies contracted power and provides lifecycle services to utilities, municipalities, independent power producers and data-center customers. ECP Fund V completed a majority investment in August 2024 from affiliates of Eos Partners and ACON Investments; founder Jeff Canon and management invested alongside ECP. Exact sponsor and management percentages and the acquisition vehicle are not publicly disclosed. PROENERGY Services is an operating identity and WattBridge is a contracted-power subsidiary or segment rather than a separate PortCo. CPS Energy acquired four plants totaling 1,632 MW for US$1.387 billion in September 2025, and STEC acquired two plants totaling 768 MW for US$768 million in April 2026. Those transactions monetized assets while PROENERGY retained service relationships and did not sell the platform. ECP and Bridgepoint continue to report PROENERGY as current, and no later company sale or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 19, 2026.

milestones.event: Jeff Canon founded PROENERGY in Sedalia, Missouri.
ECP Fund V completed a majority investment from Eos and ACON affiliates; Jeff Canon and management invested alongside ECP, and the transaction was announced September 5.

PROENERGY completed two asset-level transactions selling six Texas plants totaling 2.4 GW for an aggregate US$2.155 billion while retaining operations, maintenance and lifecycle-service relationships.

company.name: Restaurant Technologies, Inc.
company.subsector: Commercial kitchen oil management and back-of-house services
company.description: Restaurant Technologies, Inc. is a Mendota Heights, Minnesota-based route and installed-equipment infrastructure-services platform that provides closed-loop bulk cooking-oil delivery, storage, filtration, monitoring and used-oil collection, together with hood and flue services. It serves more than 45,000 U.S. customer locations through 41 depots and more than 1,200 employees. ECP completed its acquisition from Goldman Sachs Asset Management in April 2022; Continental Grain continued as an investor and Enlightened Hospitality Investments invested alongside ECP. Current company board materials retain representatives associated with all three investor groups. Exact ownership percentages, the ECP fund and acquisition vehicle are not publicly disclosed. GSAM's West Street Infrastructure Partners III had acquired the company in 2018 and exited in the 2022 transaction. Eagle Parent, Double Eagle Buyer, lenders, depots, routes and customer installations are financing entities or operating assets rather than separate owners or PortCos. No later company sale, ECP exit or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 19, 2026.

company.name: Arium Networks
company.description: Arium Networks LLC is a U.S. small-cell, distributed-antenna-system and venue-network infrastructure platform created from Crown Castle's former Small Cell business. It designs, deploys and manages outdoor and in-building wireless networks for the three largest U.S. mobile network operators and venue customers. EQT Active Core Infrastructure I announced the acquisition in March 2025 and completed it through Small Cells HoldCo Inc. on May 1, 2026, when Arium launched as a standalone company. Arium reported more than 100,000 small cells on air or under contract across 43 states at launch and is headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina. EQT continues to list Arium as current. The separately sold Crown Castle Fiber Solutions business now owned by Zayo is outside this company boundary. Public sources do not disclose one comparable EQT economic stake across the nested fund and co-investment structure, and no later platform sale, sponsor exit or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 29, 2026.

milestones.event: EQT Active Core Infrastructure signed to acquire Crown Castle's Small Cell business for approximately $4.25 billion; Crown Castle's Fiber Solutions sale to Zayo was a separate transaction.
Arium Networks was announced as the successor brand for Crown Castle's Small Cell business ahead of its standalone launch.
The sale to Small Cells HoldCo Inc. closed and Arium Networks launched as an EQT Active Core Infrastructure I portfolio company.

company.name: EdgeConneX
company.description: EdgeConneX is a global data-center developer and operator headquartered in Herndon, Virginia. Founded in 2009, it develops and operates edge, hyperscale, purpose-built and build-to-density facilities for hyperscale, cloud, enterprise, content, network, technology and AI customers. Public materials describe more than 80 operating or developing sites across over 60 markets in more than 20 countries, with over 10 GW of additional planned capacity. EQT Infrastructure IV completed the Providence-led acquisition on November 5, 2020; EQT Infrastructure V joined in 2021, Sixth Street-managed funds completed a minority investment in 2024, and EQT AI Infrastructure acquired a minority interest from EQT Infrastructure IV and V in 2026 while EQT remained the largest shareholder group. Liberty Global fully exited its former minority interest on June 29, 2026. CPP Investments' $1.75 billion commitment supports EQT's broader AI infrastructure strategy but is not disclosed as a separate direct EdgeConneX shareholding. Individual sites, campuses, subsidiaries, AdaniConneX and Chayora are outside this canonical company boundary. No later company sale, EQT exit, Sixth Street exit or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 29, 2026.

milestones.event: EQT Infrastructure IV completed the acquisition of EdgeConneX from a Providence-led investor group.
EQT Infrastructure V announced a co-investment in EdgeConneX alongside EQT Infrastructure IV; the exact closing date and percentage were not disclosed.
EQT announced that Sixth Street-managed funds had made a minority investment in EdgeConneX by acquiring interests from EQT Infrastructure IV and V.

EQT AI Infrastructure acquired a minority interest from EQT Infrastructure IV and V while EQT remained the largest shareholder group; Liberty Global fully exited its former minority interest on June 29.

company.description: Kelowna and Vernon Hospitals Project is an availability-based healthcare PPP in British Columbia whose legal ProjectCo is Infusion Health KVH General Partnership. The DBFM project covers four facilities across the Kelowna General Hospital and Vernon Jubilee Hospital campuses, together with lifecycle obligations for existing infrastructure, and operates for Interior Health under an agreement running to August 2042. BBGI completed an initial 50% acquisition on November 14, 2013 and acquired the remaining 50% on August 19, 2020; BBGI continued to describe the ProjectCo as wholly owned in April 2026. Equitix- and Dalmore-backed Jura held indirect exposure to the other 50% through JLIF from September 2018 until BBGI's 2020 acquisition. BCI's 2025 acquisition of BBGI is upstream and is not recorded as a separate ProjectCo owner. Interior Health is the public counterparty, the named hospitals are facilities, and Black & McDonald is a contractor rather than an owner. No later ProjectCo sale or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 29, 2026.

milestones.event: The Kelowna and Vernon Hospitals Project reached financial close under the Infusion Health KVH General Partnership ProjectCo.
BBGI completed its initial 50% acquisition on November 14, and JLIF completed its acquisition of the other 50% on November 28.
Jura Acquisition completed the JLIF take-private, giving the Equitix- and Dalmore-backed consortium indirect exposure to JLIF's 50% interest.
BBGI acquired the remaining 50% interest and became the 100% owner of the ProjectCo.

company.name: Live Oak Wind Farm
company.description: Live Oak Wind Farm is an operating approximately 200 MW onshore wind project in Schleicher County, Texas, held through Live Oak Wind Project, LLC and Live Oak Wind Partners, LLC. The project uses 76 Siemens Gamesa turbines and sells renewable generation into ERCOT; ENGIE remains operator. John Laing acquired a 75% sponsor interest in 2019 while ENGIE retained 25%. That 75% block later entered John Laing Investments Limited, which direct April 2026 evidence describes as 50:50 owned by Equitix and KKR-owned John Laing Group. The Equitix and KKR percentages apply to JLIL and are not recorded as inferred direct 37.5% project stakes. John Laing is preserved as the former 2019 acquirer and current KKR-owned asset manager rather than a third independent current owner. Lenders, tax-equity investors, hedging counterparties, offtakers and project subsidiaries are not separate PortCos. No later project sale or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 29, 2026.

milestones.event: Live Oak reached commercial operation as an approximately 200 MW wind project in Schleicher County, Texas.
John Laing acquired a 75% sponsor interest in Live Oak while ENGIE retained 25% and remained operator.
KKR completed the John Laing acquisition and Equitix entered the 50:50 JLIL structure that held John Laing's former 75% Live Oak block.

company.name: North Carolina Solar
company.description: North Carolina Solar is one five-project operating solar portfolio in North Carolina comprising Brantley, Fox Creek, Buckleberry, Innovative Solar 54 and Innovative Solar 67. John Laing's portfolio page reports 334 MWdc across the five assets, with contracted power sales to Duke Energy Progress and commercial operations beginning from late 2018 into early 2019. John Laing assembled the portfolio in 2018. KKR acquired John Laing Group in September 2021, and Equitix completed its 50% investment in John Laing Investments Limited on October 6, 2021. Direct April 2026 evidence describes JLIL as 50:50 owned by Equitix and KKR-owned John Laing Group. John Laing is preserved as the former sponsor and current KKR-owned asset manager, not a third independent owner. The historic 9.9% ProjectCo/HoldCo minority and its current rights are not publicly disclosed and are not inferred to be tax equity. Granite is a separate eight-project portfolio and is excluded from this company boundary. No later portfolio sale or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 29, 2026.

milestones.event: John Laing assembled the Brantley, Fox Creek, Buckleberry, Innovative Solar 54 and Innovative Solar 67 projects as one North Carolina solar portfolio.
The five-project portfolio entered commercial operation, with John Laing reporting 334 MWdc of operating solar capacity.
KKR completed the John Laing acquisition and Equitix completed its 50% JLIL investment, establishing the 50:50 JLIL ownership structure.

company.name: Ontario Science Partners General Partnership
company.subsector: DBFM cultural and science centre infrastructure
company.ownershipVehicle: John Laing Limited / Ontario Science Partners General Partnership
company.description: Ontario Science Partners General Partnership is the ProjectCo delivering the new Ontario Science Centre at Ontario Place in Toronto under a C$1.04 billion design-build-finance-maintain concession. The approximately 400,000-square-foot scope includes the new centre and rehabilitation of the Cinesphere and Pods, followed by a 30-year maintenance term. The ProjectCo reached financial close on February 11, 2026 with John Laing holding 64%, Sacyr Infrastructure Canada 26% and Amico Major Projects 10%. John Laing's interest is attributed to KKR because the 2021 takeover terms reserved all future John Laing investments to KKR; the project is outside the legacy JLIL/Equitix portfolio. Construction began in May 2026 with opening targeted for 2029, and no later sale or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 29, 2026.

milestones.event: Ontario Science Partners General Partnership was created as the project entity for the new Ontario Science Centre DBFM concession.
The ProjectCo reached financial close with John Laing at 64%, Sacyr Infrastructure Canada at 26% and Amico Major Projects at 10%.
Infrastructure Ontario and the sponsors announced the C$1.04 billion fixed-price DBFM award and 30-year maintenance term.
Construction commenced at Ontario Place, with opening of the new centre targeted for 2029.

company.name: Surrey Pretrial Services Centre Expansion Project
company.description: Surrey Pretrial Services Centre Expansion Project is an availability-based correctional-facility PPP in Surrey, British Columbia, delivered through Brookfield Infrastructure Partnerships Surrey. The DBFM concession covers a 216-cell expansion, renovations to the existing facility and long-term facilities maintenance for the provincial corrections system, with concession expiry on October 31, 2043. Brookfield and Forum were the original 2011 sponsors; Forum consolidated Brookfield's interests in 2015; and Fiera Infrastructure acquired 100% on April 19, 2016. Fiera continues to list Surrey as an unrealized Woodford Social Infrastructure investment under EagleCrest Infrastructure Canada LP. Surrey was not in JLIF's complete pre-takeover portfolio, so Equitix, Dalmore and Jura did not acquire it in 2018. No later sale or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 29, 2026.

milestones.event: The concession reached financial close with Brookfield- and Forum-linked entities as the ProjectCo partners.
Construction of the 216-cell expansion and associated renovations was completed.
Forum announced that it had recently completed the acquisition of Brookfield's project interests and asset-management rights.
Fiera Infrastructure completed its acquisition of a 100% equity interest and placed the project in its Woodford Social Infrastructure portfolio.

company.name: Cardinal Portfolio JV
company.subsector: Operating utility-scale and distributed solar portfolio
company.description: Cardinal Portfolio JV is a 50/50 operating-solar joint venture between Clearway Energy, Inc. and Fengate-managed vehicles. The ring-fenced portfolio comprises 12 reported projects across California, New Mexico and Colorado totaling approximately 225-227 MW, including utility-scale and distributed-generation facilities placed in service between 2010 and 2017. Clearway and Fengate signed the cash membership-interest purchase agreement on October 3, 2025, received FERC authorization on March 19, 2026 and closed on March 30, 2026. Fengate attributes its interest to Fengate Infrastructure Yield Fund and affiliates, including LiUNA participation. The JV is the western operating subset of the broader Cardinal transaction, not the full 610-613 MW Cardinal portfolio or the broader Clearway platform. No later owner exit or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 29, 2026.

canonicalAfterImage.description: Cardinal Portfolio JV is a 50/50 operating-solar joint venture between Clearway Energy, Inc. and Fengate-managed vehicles. The ring-fenced portfolio comprises 12 reported projects across California, New Mexico and Colorado totaling approximately 225-227 MW, including utility-scale and distributed-generation facilities placed in service between 2010 and 2017. Clearway and Fengate signed the cash membership-interest purchase agreement on October 3, 2025, received FERC authorization on March 19, 2026 and closed on March 30, 2026. Fengate attributes its interest to Fengate Infrastructure Yield Fund and affiliates, including LiUNA participation. The JV is the western operating subset of the broader Cardinal transaction, not the full 610-613 MW Cardinal portfolio or the broader Clearway platform. No later owner exit or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 29, 2026.

company.name: Health Park at Avenir
company.subsector: Healthcare development and medical office real estate
company.description: Health Park at Avenir is an investor-owned healthcare development in Palm Beach Gardens, Florida, held through SFG PBG Medical, LLC. The bounded initial phase comprises an approximately 53,000-square-foot neighborhood hospital and approximately 47,000-square-foot medical office building that are fully pre-leased to Jupiter Medical Center for 15 years. Fengate Infrastructure Fund IV and affiliated entities invested alongside Stonemont Financial Group and The Sina Companies; public sources do not disclose the partners' percentages. The ProjectCo closed its land acquisition and construction financing before the June 24, 2026 groundbreaking, with opening targeted for early 2028. Jupiter Medical Center is the tenant/operator, Sina is an owner/developer, and later medical-office phases are excluded until common ownership is proven. No later sale or signed ownership transaction was identified through August 29, 2026.

company.description: Fengate-MedCraft Cleveland Clinic Outpatient Portfolio is a 24-facility medical-outpatient sale-leaseback portfolio across Ohio and Florida totaling more than 900,000 square feet. Fengate Asset Management and MedCraft Healthcare Real Estate acquired the portfolio in September 2025 through FG MC II Cleveland, LLC and location-specific title entities; public sources do not disclose their percentages or a deal-specific Fengate fund. The portfolio is the first Fengate-MedCraft joint-venture acquisition and is distinct from Fengate's separate Project Lotus investment with Montecito. No later disposal, recapitalization, owner exit or signed ownership transaction was identified through August 29, 2026.

company.name: Montecito Medical Outpatient Portfolio
company.description: Montecito Medical Outpatient Portfolio is the bounded 2025 Project Lotus sale-recapitalization of a national medical-outpatient portfolio. Fengate Asset Management invested through Fengate Infrastructure Fund IV and affiliated entities using FG MNTO I LOTUS, LLC, while Montecito Medical Real Estate retained equity; their percentages are not publicly disclosed. Fengate described 16 facilities in 10 states, while transaction-advisor and trade sources described 18 properties in 11 states totaling approximately 750,000 square feet and a US$323 million recapitalization with US$233 million of financing. The facilities were 100% leased at closing to health systems and physician groups. The record excludes Montecito's enterprise portfolio and Fengate's separate MedCraft/Cleveland Clinic portfolio. No later portfolio sale, owner exit or signed ownership transaction was identified through August 29, 2026.

company.name: Prince George's County Blueprint Schools Program (Phase One)
company.description: Prince George's County Blueprint Schools Program (Phase One) is an availability-based DBFM concession covering six public schools in Prince George's County, Maryland through Prince George's County Education & Community Partners, LLC. The ProjectCo reached financial close on December 18, 2020 with Fengate-controlled entities holding 75% and Gilbane Development holding 25%. Five middle schools opened in August 2023 and Colin L. Powell K-8 Academy opened in November 2023; lifecycle and facilities-management services continue under a term ending June 30, 2053. BBGI acquired 100% from the Fengate and Gilbane vehicles in February 2026 and remains the current owner; BCI's ownership of BBGI is upstream and is not added as a separate ProjectCo owner. Phase Two is a distinct project. No later sale, concession termination or signed ownership transaction was identified through August 29, 2026.

company.name: Cambrian Innovation
company.subsector: Industrial water reuse and wastewater treatment
company.description: Cambrian Innovation, Inc. develops, owns and operates distributed industrial wastewater treatment, water-reuse and energy-recovery infrastructure through service-based Water-Energy Purchase Agreement structures. Pennybacker-affiliated funds acquired Cambrian on November 16, 2023 and committed up to US$200 million of growth equity; current company materials continue to identify Pennybacker as the corporate owner. Generate Capital's earlier participation concerned project-level WEPA financing and jointly owned project vehicles beginning in 2015, not current corporate ownership, and its exact project-SPV stake and exit date were not publicly disclosed. Cambrian announced a US$150 million ING credit facility in June 2025 to expand its active infrastructure portfolio; that facility is debt. No later corporate sale or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 29, 2026.

company.name: CleanCapital Holdings, LLC
company.description: CleanCapital Holdings, LLC develops, acquires, owns and operates distributed solar and energy-storage projects across the United States. Founded in 2015 and headquartered in New York, the platform serves commercial, industrial, institutional, utility and public-sector counterparties through contracted clean-energy assets. Generate Capital and CleanCapital established a project-acquisition warehouse in 2017 targeting approximately US$300 million of operating clean-energy assets; this was project-level financing and ownership rather than disclosed corporate equity, and Generate's exact project stake and exit date were not publicly disclosed. BlackRock Renewable Power Group funds made a direct corporate investment in 2019, but that period is historical. Manulife Investment Management made a corporate investment in 2021 through Manulife Infrastructure Fund II and remains the only named current institutional backer. The exact Manulife and former BlackRock percentages are not publicly disclosed. Infranity's January 2026 capital is a holdco debt facility, and no platform sale or signed ownership exit was identified through August 29, 2026.

milestones.event: CleanCapital was founded.
CleanCapital and Generate announced a project-acquisition warehouse targeting approximately US$300 million of operating clean-energy assets, initially focused on distributed solar.
Funds managed by BlackRock's Renewable Power Group made a direct investment in CleanCapital; the exact fund, stake and later exit timing were not publicly disclosed.
Manulife Investment Management made a corporate investment and US$300 million commitment; CleanCapital also became sole owner of the 46.9 MW portfolio previously financed with BlackRock.
CleanCapital acquired a 40-asset, 22.7 MW portfolio from Kendall Sustainable Infrastructure and secured further equity investment.
CleanCapital announced the acquisition of a 25 MWh storage portfolio from Pacifico.
CleanCapital secured a US$300 million holdco debt facility with Infranity to support distributed-generation growth; the financing did not create a new equity owner.

canonicalAfterImage.name: CleanCapital Holdings, LLC
canonicalAfterImage.description: CleanCapital Holdings, LLC develops, acquires, owns and operates distributed solar and energy-storage projects across the United States. Founded in 2015 and headquartered in New York, the platform serves commercial, industrial, institutional, utility and public-sector counterparties through contracted clean-energy assets. Generate Capital and CleanCapital established a project-acquisition warehouse in 2017 targeting approximately US$300 million of operating clean-energy assets; this was project-level financing and ownership rather than disclosed corporate equity, and Generate's exact project stake and exit date were not publicly disclosed. BlackRock Renewable Power Group funds made a direct corporate investment in 2019, but that period is historical. Manulife Investment Management made a corporate investment in 2021 through Manulife Infrastructure Fund II and remains the only named current institutional backer. The exact Manulife and former BlackRock percentages are not publicly disclosed. Infranity's January 2026 capital is a holdco debt facility, and no platform sale or signed ownership exit was identified through August 29, 2026.

company.subsector: Fuel cell and hydrogen equipment financing
company.ownershipVehicle: Generate Lending LLC / Generate PPL SPV I, LLC secured debt facility
company.description: Plug Power Fuel Cell Asset SPVs is an archived generic financing construct rather than a manager-level operating portfolio company. Plug Power filings document separate sale-leaseback lessors that held title to specified fuel-cell equipment beginning in 2016-2017, followed by a US$100 million secured Generate Lending facility announced in 2019. The Generate loan was debt rather than equity and Plug Power reported repaying it in full in December 2022. Public filings reviewed through August 29, 2026 did not identify an equity conversion, foreclosure, renewed Generate ownership or a current consolidated Generate-owned Plug Power SPV platform. The exact residual disposition of every historical leased-equipment vehicle was not publicly disclosed, but that gap does not support retaining this generic row as an active direct infrastructure holding.

milestones.event: Plug Power entered equipment sale-leaseback structures in which separate lessor SPVs held title to specified deployed fuel-cell systems.

Generate Lending provided a secured debt facility in April 2019; Plug Power reported repaying the loan in full in December 2022, ending the disclosed Generate credit exposure without an equity conversion.

company.name: Generate–Stem LCR
company.ownershipVehicle: SPV IV Class A managing interest; exact Generate affiliate not publicly disclosed
company.description: Generate-Stem LCR, LLC is a Delaware special-purpose vehicle formed on June 30, 2017 to purchase and own behind-the-meter battery-storage systems supporting Southern California Edison's West Los Angeles Basin local-capacity program. Stem, Inc. holds a 50% Class B non-managing interest and remains the host-facing technology and operating counterparty. Stem's filings describe a two-class structure and its 50% interest, so the Generate-linked Class A managing interest is recorded as an inferred 50%; the exact Generate affiliate and fund are not publicly disclosed. The cited 85 MW / 340 MWh figures are contract and funding ceilings rather than verified deployed capacity. Stem continued to report obligations and repayments for its consolidated SPE program through June 30, 2026, and no sale, transfer, foreclosure, dissolution or signed pending ownership transaction for Generate-Stem LCR was identified through August 29, 2026.

milestones.event: Generate-Stem LCR, LLC was formed as SPV IV with Class A managing and Class B non-managing membership interests to purchase and own Southern California behind-the-meter storage systems; Stem retained the 50% Class B interest.
Stem continued to report obligations and repayments for its special-purpose storage program, with no disclosed sale, transfer or Generate-Stem LCR exit.

company.name: ACES Delta, LLC
company.description: ACES Delta, LLC is a clean-hydrogen production and underground salt-cavern storage platform in Delta, Utah. The 2019 joint venture is currently owned by Chevron-controlled Magnum Development, LLC as majority owner and Mitsubishi Power Americas, Inc. as minority owner; exact percentages are not publicly disclosed. Haddington Energy Partners III formerly owned the platform indirectly through Magnum and exited that position when Chevron acquired 100% of Magnum in 2023. Haddington ESP I separately manages construction equity in the ACES I project company, while GIC, Ontario Teachers', AIMCo and Manulife are investors in that fund rather than verified direct ACES Delta owners. The first stage comprises 220 MW of electrolysis and two salt caverns supporting more than 300 GWh of storage. All 40 electrolyzers were reported commissioned in the first quarter of 2026, with final start-up still expected later in 2026. No later platform sale or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 29, 2026.

milestones.event: Magnum Development and Mitsubishi Hitachi Power Systems announced the Advanced Clean Energy Storage joint venture that became ACES Delta.
The U.S. Department of Energy closed a US$504.4 million loan guarantee for the ACES I hydrogen-production and storage project; the facility is debt rather than equity ownership.

Haddington announced US$650 million of commitments to Haddington ESP I from GIC, Ontario Teachers', AIMCo and Manulife; the institutions invested as fund LPs, not as disclosed direct ACES Delta owners.
Chevron acquired 100% of Magnum Development from Haddington, obtaining a majority interest in ACES Delta; Mitsubishi Power Americas remained the minority joint-venture owner.
HydrogenPro reported that all 40 electrolyzers comprising the 220 MW first stage had been commissioned, while final project start-up remained expected in the second half of 2026.

company.name: Direct ChassisLink, Inc. (DCLI)
company.ownershipVehicle: Epsom Investment Pte. Ltd. via DCLI BidCo LLC
company.description: Direct ChassisLink, Inc. (DCLI) leases and manages marine and domestic intermodal chassis used to move containerized freight through more than 500 U.S. port and rail locations. The Charlotte-based platform serves ocean carriers, railroads, motor carriers, beneficial cargo owners, shippers and logistics providers and reports a fleet of approximately 290,000 chassis. GIC, OMERS Infrastructure and Wren House Infrastructure completed their joint acquisition on December 13, 2022; public materials identify the consortium as current but do not disclose member percentages, so no equal split is inferred. DCLI's former ownership chain includes Maersk, Littlejohn, EQT Infrastructure and Apollo-managed funds. The production database already redirects the retired duplicate production ID to this canonical company; this proposal also retires the reciprocal Direct ChassisLink, Inc. seed identity. No later sale or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 29, 2026.

milestones.event: Maersk established the chassis-leasing predecessor that later became Direct ChassisLink.
The business launched the Direct ChassisLink identity and began expanding its U.S. chassis-leasing platform.
Littlejohn & Co. completed its acquisition of Direct ChassisLink from Maersk, establishing DCLI as an independent portfolio company.
EQT Infrastructure acquired DCLI from Littlejohn and became the controlling owner.
Apollo-managed funds acquired control of DCLI; EQT retained a 20% minority interest.
GIC, OMERS Infrastructure and Wren House announced an agreement to acquire DCLI from Apollo- and EQT-managed funds.
The GIC, OMERS Infrastructure and Wren House consortium completed its joint acquisition of DCLI; Apollo and EQT exited.
DCLI refinanced through its BidCo structure while continuing to operate under the same three-owner consortium; the financing did not change platform ownership.

Apollo-managed funds acquired control of DCLI; EQT retained a 20% minority interest.
GIC, OMERS Infrastructure and Wren House announced an agreement to acquire DCLI from Apollo- and EQT-managed funds.
The GIC, OMERS Infrastructure and Wren House consortium completed its joint acquisition of DCLI; Apollo and EQT exited.
DCLI refinanced through its BidCo structure while continuing to operate under the same three-owner consortium; the financing did not change platform ownership.
